title.raw: 卷36 李順 Volume 36: Li Shun

sentences.zh: 李順，字德正，趙郡平棘人也。

translations.literal: Li Shun, styled Dezheng, was a native of Pingji in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun, whose courtesy name was Dezheng, came from Pingji in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父系，慕容垂散騎侍郎，東武城令，治有能名。

translations.literal: His father Xi served Murong Chui as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and as magistrate of Dongwucheng; in governance he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi had been a Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary under Murong Chui and magistrate of Dongwucheng, where his able rule won him renown.

sentences.zh: 太祖定中原，以系為平棘令。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor settled the Central Plains, he appointed Xi magistrate of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu pacified the Central Plains, he made Xi magistrate of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 年老，卒於家。

translations.literal: In old age he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He grew old and died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈寧朔將軍、趙郡太守、平棘男。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the North, Administrator of Zhao Commandery, and Baron of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the titles General Who Pacifies the North, Administrator of Zhao Commandery, and Baron of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 順博涉經史，有才策，知名於世。

translations.literal: Shun ranged broadly through the classics and histories, had talent and stratagems, and was known in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Shun read deeply in the classics and histories, possessed talent and strategic insight, and was renowned among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 神瑞中，中書博士，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Shenrui era he was Doctor of the Secretariat, then transferred to Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenrui reign he served as Doctor of the Secretariat, then was promoted to Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 始光初，從征蠕蠕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shiguang he followed the campaign against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening year of Shiguang he joined the expedition against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 以籌略之功，拜後軍將軍，仍賜爵平棘子，加奮威將軍。

translations.literal: For achievements in planning strategy he was appointed General of the Rear Army, and was also enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingji with the additional title General of Inspiring Might.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his strategic counsel he was named General of the Rear Army, enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingji, and given the additional rank of General of Inspiring Might.

sentences.zh: 世祖將討赫連昌，謂崔浩曰：「朕前北征，李順獻策數事，實合經略大謀。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor was about to attack Helian Chang and said to Cui Hao: "On my earlier northern expedition Li Shun offered several plans that truly fit grand strategic design.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu prepared to campaign against Helian Chang, he said to Cui Hao, "On my last northern campaign Li Shun proposed several measures that truly matched a comprehensive strategy.

sentences.zh: 今欲使總攝前驅之事，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: Now I wish to have him oversee the vanguard affairs—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I now want him to take charge of the advance forces—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「順智足周務，實如聖旨。

translations.literal: " Hao replied: "Shun's wisdom suffices to handle all affairs—this truly accords with Your Majesty's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao answered, "Shun's intelligence is equal to every task—that is exactly as Your Majesty says.

sentences.zh: 但臣與之婚姻，深知其行，然性果於去就，不可專委。

translations.literal: But I am related to him by marriage and know his conduct well; yet his nature is decisive in staying or leaving, and he cannot be entrusted with sole authority."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am bound to him by marriage and know his ways well; he is too quick to choose his own course, and sole command should not be placed in his hands."

sentences.zh: 」世祖乃止。

translations.literal: " The Shizu Emperor thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 初浩弟娶順妹，又以弟子娶順女，雖二門婚媾，而浩頗輕順，順又弗之伏也。

translations.literal: Earlier Hao's younger brother had married Shun's sister, and Hao's nephew had married Shun's daughter; though the two families were joined by marriage, Hao rather looked down on Shun, and Shun in turn would not submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hao's brother had married Shun's sister, and Hao's nephew had married Shun's daughter. Though the two houses were linked by marriage, Hao tended to slight Shun, and Shun refused to defer to him.

sentences.zh: 由是潛相猜忌，故浩毀之。

translations.literal: Because of this they secretly mistrusted each other, and so Hao slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore nursed a private mutual suspicion, and Hao spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 至統萬，大破昌軍，順謀功居右，轉拜左軍將軍。

translations.literal: At Tongwan they routed Chang's army; Shun's planning merit ranked highest, and he was transferred and appointed General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongwan they smashed Chang's forces; Shun's strategic contribution stood first, and he was promoted to General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 後征統萬，遷前將軍，授之以兵。

translations.literal: Later, on the campaign against Tongwan, he was moved to General of the Van and given command of troops.
translations.idiomatic: On a later expedition against Tongwan he was made General of the Van and entrusted with troops.

sentences.zh: 昌出逆戰，順督勒士眾，破其左軍。

translations.literal: Chang came out to give battle; Shun directed and urged the troops and broke his left wing.
translations.idiomatic: Chang marched out to meet them; Shun rallied the men and shattered his left wing.

sentences.zh: 及克統萬，世祖賜諸將珍寶雜物，順固辭，唯取書數千卷。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was taken, the Shizu Emperor bestowed treasures and sundry goods on the generals; Shun firmly declined and took only several thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongwan fell, the emperor gave the generals jewels and other gifts; Shun steadfastly refused all but a few thousand volumes of books.

sentences.zh: 世祖善之。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 至京論功，以順為給事黃門侍郎，賜奴婢十五戶，帛千匹。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital to assess merit, Shun was made Attendant at the Gates of the Yellow Gate with duties in the Secretariat, and granted fifteen households of slaves and a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, when rewards were apportioned, Shun was appointed Attendant at the Gates of the Yellow Gate with secretariat duties, given fifteen households of bondsmen, and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又從擊赫連定於平涼。

translations.literal: He again followed in the attack on Helian Ding at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in the assault on Helian Ding at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 三秦平，遷散騎常侍，進爵為侯，加征虜將軍，遷四部尚書，甚見寵待。

translations.literal: When the Three Qins were pacified, he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Cavalier, advanced in rank to marquis, given the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians, moved to Director of the Four Departments, and greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Qins were pacified he became Regular Attendant of the Cavalier, was raised to marquis, given the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians, and appointed Director of the Four Departments, enjoying exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜以河西內附，世祖欲精簡行人，崔浩曰：「蒙遜稱蕃，款著河右，若俾遐域流通，殊荒畢至，宜令清德重臣奉詔褒慰，尚書李順即其人也。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun submitted the Hexi region to the court; the Shizu Emperor wished to select envoys carefully. Cui Hao said: "Mengxun has declared himself a vassal and his sincerity is evident west of the Yellow River. If we are to let distant regions communicate and all far barbarian lands come, we should send a minister of pure virtue and weight to bear the edict in praise and comfort—Director Li Shun is such a man."
translations.idiomatic: When Juqu Mengxun brought the Hexi west under allegiance, the emperor wanted to choose his envoys with care. Cui Hao said, "Mengxun has declared vassalage and shown good faith on the western frontier. To open channels to distant lands and draw in every remote realm, we should send a man of sterling character and high standing to convey the imperial message of praise and reassurance—Director Li Shun is the man."

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「順納言大臣，固不宜先為此使。

translations.literal: " The Shizu Emperor said: "Shun is a great minister who speaks at court—he is certainly not fit to go first on such a mission.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Shun is a chief minister of the realm—he is hardly the man to send on this errand in the first place.

sentences.zh: 若蒙遜身執玉帛而朝於朕，復何以加之？

translations.literal: If Mengxun himself comes bearing jade and silk to pay court to me, what further honor could I add?"
translations.idiomatic: If Mengxun should come in person with tribute to attend my court, what further reward could I bestow?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「邢貞使吳，亦魏之太常。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Xing Zhen's mission to Wu was also undertaken by Wei as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied, "When Xing Zhen went to Wu, he too went as Grand Master of Ceremonies of Wei.

sentences.zh: 苟事是宜，無嫌於重。

translations.literal: If the affair is fitting, there is no objection on grounds of rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the task requires it, rank should not stand in the way.

sentences.zh: 爾日之行，豈吳王入覲也。

translations.literal: The journey of that day—was it the King of Wu coming to audience?"
translations.idiomatic: That mission was hardly the King of Wu coming to pay homage."

sentences.zh: 」世祖從之，以順為太常，策拜蒙遜為太傅、涼王。

translations.literal: " The Shizu Emperor followed this advice, appointed Shun Grand Master of Ceremonies, and by edict enfeoffed Mengxun as Grand Tutor and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his counsel, made Shun Grand Master of Ceremonies, and issued an edict enfeoffing Mengxun as Grand Tutor and King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜使持節、都督秦雍梁益四州諸軍事、寧西將軍、開府、長安鎮都大將，進爵高平公。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qin, Yong, Liang, and Yi, General Who Pacifies the West, with an open office, and Grand General commanding the garrison of Chang'an; his rank was advanced to Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from the embassy he received the staff of authority as commander of Qin, Yong, Liang, and Yi, the title General Who Pacifies the West, an open office, and the post of grand general commanding Chang'an; he was raised to Duke of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復徵為四部尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned as Director of the Four Departments with the additional title Regular Attendant of the Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled to the capital as Director of the Four Departments with the additional rank of Regular Attendant of the Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 延和初，復使涼州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanhe he was again sent to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening year of Yanhe he was dispatched to Liang Province once more.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜遣中兵校郎楊定歸白順曰：「年衰多疹，舊患發動，腰脚不隨，不堪拜伏。

translations.literal: Mengxun sent the Central Army Commandant Yang Dinggui to inform Shun: "I am aged and afflicted with many ailments; old complaints have flared up, my waist and legs do not obey me, and I cannot bear to bow prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun sent his Central Army Commandant Yang Dinggui to tell Shun, "I am old and plagued by illness; old troubles have returned, my back and legs will not serve me, and I cannot kneel and bow.

sentences.zh: 比三五日，消息小差，當相見。

translations.literal: In about three to five days, when my condition improves slightly, we shall meet."
translations.idiomatic: In three or five days, when I am somewhat better, we shall meet."

sentences.zh: 」順曰：「王之年老，朝廷所知。

translations.literal: " Shun said: "Your Majesty's advanced age is known to the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun replied, "Your Majesty's age is no secret to the court.

sentences.zh: 以王祗執臣禮，別有詔旨，豈得自安不見上使也。

translations.literal: Because Your Majesty reverently observes the rites of a subject, there is a separate imperial edict—how can you rest at ease and refuse to receive the envoy from above?"
translations.idiomatic: Because you hold yourself to the rites of a subject, a special edict has been issued—how can you take your ease and refuse to receive the emperor's envoy?"

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜翌日延順入，至庭中，而蒙遜箕坐隱几，無動起之狀。

translations.literal: " The next day Mengxun invited Shun in; when Shun reached the courtyard, Mengxun sat with legs spread astride, leaning on a armrest, showing no sign of rising.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Mengxun received him. Shun entered the courtyard, but Mengxun sat sprawled on his couch with legs apart and gave no sign of rising.

sentences.zh: 順正色大言曰：「不謂此叟無禮乃至於是！

translations.literal: Shun, with stern countenance, spoke loudly: "I did not expect this old man to be so devoid of propriety!
translations.idiomatic: Shun set his face and spoke in a loud voice: "I never thought this old fellow could be so shameless!

sentences.zh: 今則覆亡之不恤，而敢陵侮天地。

translations.literal: Now, when ruin is at hand and you do not care, you still dare to insult Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: You stand on the brink of destruction yet show no concern, and still dare to insult Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 魂神逝矣，何用見之。

translations.literal: Your spirit has departed—what use is there in meeting you?"
translations.idiomatic: Your soul has already fled—why should I stay to see you?"

sentences.zh: 」將握節而出。

translations.literal: " He was about to grasp his staff and leave.
translations.idiomatic: " He took up his staff of office to depart.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜使定歸追順於庭曰：「太常既雅恕衰疾，傳云朝廷有不拜之詔，是以敢自安耳。

translations.literal: Mengxun sent Dinggui after Shun in the courtyard, saying: "The Grand Master of Ceremonies has graciously forgiven my age and illness; it is reported that the court has an edict exempting one from bowing—that is why I dared to rest at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun sent Dinggui running after him in the courtyard: "The Grand Master has kindly excused my age and infirmity; word came that the court had issued an edict waiving the bow—that is why I presumed to remain seated.

sentences.zh: 若太常曰：『爾拜爾跽，而不祗命。

translations.literal: If the Grand Master of Ceremonies says, 'You shall bow and kneel,' yet I do not reverently obey the command,
translations.idiomatic: If the Grand Master says, 'Bow and kneel,' and I do not obey,

sentences.zh: 』斯乃小臣之罪矣。

translations.literal: ' then that is the fault of this petty minister."
translations.idiomatic: then the fault is mine alone."

sentences.zh: 」順益怒曰：「齊桓公九合諸侯，一匡天下，周王賜胙，命曰：伯舅無下拜。

translations.literal: " Shun grew still angrier and said: "Duke Huan of Qi nine times assembled the feudal lords and set the realm in order; the King of Zhou granted sacrificial meat with the command: 'Uncle, do not bow down.'
translations.idiomatic: " Shun's anger rose further: "Duke Huan of Qi nine times gathered the lords and set the world in order. The Zhou king granted him sacrificial meat with the words, 'Uncle, need not bow down.'

sentences.zh: 而桓公奉遵臣節，降而拜受。

translations.literal: Yet Duke Huan reverently observed the rites of a subject, descended, and bowed to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huan still observed the rites of a subject, stepped down, and bowed to receive it.

sentences.zh: 今君雖功高勳厚，未若小白之勤朝廷，雖相崇重，未有不拜之詔。

translations.literal: Now though Your Majesty's merit is high and your achievements thick, you do not equal Xiaobai's diligence toward the court; though you are honored in rank, there is no edict exempting you from bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Your merit and honors, great as they are, do not match Duke Huan's service to the throne; however highly you are esteemed, no edict has freed you from the bow.

sentences.zh: 如便偃蹇自大，此乃速禍之道，非圖久安之計。

translations.literal: If you at once become arrogant and self-important, this is the path to swift disaster, not a plan for lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on haughty defiance, you are choosing a swift road to ruin, not a policy for lasting security.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷震怒，遂相吞滅，悔何及哉！

translations.literal: If the court is shaken to anger and proceeds to swallow you up, regret will come too late!"
translations.idiomatic: If the court's wrath is roused and it moves to destroy you, remorse will come too late!"

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜曰：「太常規之以古烈，懼之以天威，敢不翹悚，敬聽休命。

translations.literal: " Mengxun said: "The Grand Master of Ceremonies has admonished me with ancient exemplars and awed me with Heaven's majesty—how dare I not stand in trembling respect and reverently heed your gracious words."
translations.idiomatic: " Mengxun said, "The Grand Master has lectured me with the heroes of old and warned me with Heaven's majesty—how could I not stand in awe and heed your counsel?"

sentences.zh: 」遂拜伏盡禮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he bowed prostrate and performed the full rites.
translations.idiomatic: " He then prostrated himself and performed every courtesy.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，蒙遜曰：「夫恃德者昌，恃力者亡。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, Mengxun said: "He who relies on virtue flourishes; he who relies on force perishes.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremonies ended, Mengxun said, "Those who rely on virtue prosper; those who rely on force perish.

sentences.zh: 朝廷頃來征伐屢克，境宇已博，但當循理此民，亦足興治。

translations.literal: The court in recent times has repeatedly conquered in its campaigns and its territory is already broad; it need only govern these people according to principle, and that would suffice to raise good order.
translations.idiomatic: The court has won battle after battle and its domain is already vast; if it would only govern these people rightly, that alone would be enough to bring order.

sentences.zh: 然專務討擊，恐不可常勝。

translations.literal: Yet to devote oneself solely to punitive strikes— I fear one cannot always be victorious."
translations.idiomatic: Yet to pursue nothing but conquest—I fear victory cannot last forever."

sentences.zh: 」順曰：「昔太祖廓定洪基，造有區夏。

translations.literal: " Shun said: "In former times the Taizu Emperor broadened and settled the great foundation and created possession of the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun replied, "Long ago Taizu laid the great foundation and won the Central Realm.

sentences.zh: 太宗承統，王業惟新。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor inherited the succession, and the royal enterprise was made new.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took up the succession and renewed the royal enterprise.

sentences.zh: 自聖上臨御，志寧四海。

translations.literal: Since the Sage Emperor took the throne, his will has been to bring peace to the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Since the present sage emperor ascended the throne, his aim has been to pacify all within the seas.

sentences.zh: 是以戎車屢駕，親冒風霜，滅赫連於三秦，走蠕蠕於漠北。

translations.literal: Therefore the war chariot has been driven out repeatedly; he has personally braved wind and frost, destroyed the Helian in the Three Qins, and driven the Rouran beyond the northern deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the war chariots have rolled out again and again; he has himself braved wind and frost, destroyed the Helian in the Three Qins, and driven the Rouran beyond the northern wastes.

sentences.zh: 闢土開邊，隸首不紀；

translations.literal: He has opened land and extended borders beyond counting of heads;
translations.idiomatic: He has opened lands and pushed the frontier beyond numbering;

sentences.zh: 僵屍截馘，所在成觀。

translations.literal: stiff corpses and severed ears lie everywhere as sights to behold.
translations.idiomatic: corpses and severed ears lie heaped wherever one looks.

sentences.zh: 除蕩暴虐，存卹黎庶，威震八荒，聲被九域。

translations.literal: He has swept away cruelty and violence, preserved and comforted the common people; his might shakes the eight wilds, his fame reaches the nine regions.
translations.idiomatic: He has swept away tyranny and succored the people; his might shakes the eight directions, his fame reaches the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，用兵之美，未有今日之盛。

translations.literal: From antiquity until now, in the excellence of employing arms, none has equaled today's grandeur.
translations.idiomatic: Never in history has the art of war been displayed on so magnificent a scale as today.

sentences.zh: 是以遐方荒俗之氓，莫不翹足抗手，斂衽屈膝。

translations.literal: Therefore the people of distant regions and barbarian customs—none fail to stand on tiptoe with hands joined, gather their robes, and bend the knee.
translations.idiomatic: That is why folk of the farthest wilds all stand eager with folded hands, straighten their robes, and bend the knee.

sentences.zh: 天兵四臨，昭德罰罪，何云恃力？

translations.literal: Heaven's armies press from four sides, displaying virtue and punishing crime—how can you speak of relying on force?"
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Heaven press on every side, proclaiming virtue and punishing guilt—how can you call that mere reliance on force?"

sentences.zh: 夫聖王之用兵也，征南蠻則北狄怨，討西戎則東夷恨，天子安得已哉？

translations.literal: When a sage king employs arms, if he campaigns against the southern barbarians the northern Di resent it; if he chastises the western Rong the eastern Yi are aggrieved—how can the Son of Heaven stop of his own accord?"
translations.idiomatic: When a sage king takes up arms, campaigning against the southern barbarians stirs resentment in the north; chastising the western Rong stirs anger in the east—how can the Son of Heaven simply desist?"

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜曰：「誠如來言，則涼土之民，亦願魏帝遠至，何為復遽驛告警，不舍晝夜？

translations.literal: " Mengxun said: "If it is truly as you say, then the people of Liang ought also to long for the Wei Emperor to come from afar—why then do you again send urgent couriers with alarms day and night without cease?
translations.idiomatic: " Mengxun said, "If that is truly so, the people of Liang should welcome the Wei emperor from afar—why then do urgent dispatches fly day and night without pause?

sentences.zh: 意君之所言，殆為虛事。

translations.literal: I suspect what you say is largely empty talk."
translations.idiomatic: I suspect your words are largely empty."

sentences.zh: 」順曰：「苗民叛帝舜而親暴君，有扈違后啟而從逆主。

translations.literal: " Shun said: "The Miao people rebelled against Emperor Shun and embraced a tyrant; Youhu defied Queen Qi and followed a rebellious lord.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun said, "The Miao rebelled against Shun and embraced a tyrant; Youhu defied Qi and followed a rebel.

sentences.zh: 咸懾逼於近地，牽制於凶威，自古而然，豈獨涼民也。」

translations.literal: All were cowed and pressed by proximity, constrained by fierce power—it has been so since antiquity; how could it be only the people of Liang?"
translations.idiomatic: All were cowed by neighbors at hand and held in check by brutal force—it has always been so; why should the people of Liang alone be different?"

sentences.zh: 順既使還，世祖問與蒙遜往復之辭，及蒙遜政教得失。

translations.literal: After Shun returned from his mission, the Shizu Emperor asked about his exchanges with Mengxun and about the strengths and failings of Mengxun's government and teachings.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun returned from his embassy, the emperor asked about his exchanges with Mengxun and about the strengths and failings of Mengxun's rule.

sentences.zh: 順曰：「蒙遜專威河右三十許年，經涉艱難，粗識機變，又綏集荒陬，遠人頗亦畏服，雖不能貽厥孫謀，猶足以終其一世。

translations.literal: Shun said: "Mengxun has held sole power west of the Yellow River for some thirty years, passed through hardships, and has a rough knowledge of shifting circumstances; he has also pacified and gathered the remote borderlands, and men from afar are rather in awe and submission. Though he cannot bequeath plans to his descendants, he is still enough to finish out his own lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Mengxun has ruled the west of the river alone for some thirty years. He has weathered hardship and knows something of changing circumstances; he has also pacified the remote marches, and distant peoples largely fear and obey him. He may not leave counsel for his heirs, but he can still hold power through his own lifetime.

sentences.zh: 前歲表許十月送曇無讖，及臣往迎，便乖本意。

translations.literal: The year before last he memorialized promising to send Dharmarakṣa in the tenth month; when I went to receive him, he went against his original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Two years ago he pledged in a memorial to send Dharmarakṣa in the tenth month; when I went to receive him, he broke his word.

sentences.zh: 不忠不信，於是而甚。

translations.literal: Disloyalty and untrustworthiness—here they are at their worst.
translations.idiomatic: His disloyalty and faithlessness have reached their height.

sentences.zh: 禮者身之輿，敬者行之本。

translations.literal: Rites are the carriage of the person; reverence is the root of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is the carriage of the self; reverence is the root of action.

sentences.zh: 未有無禮不敬而能久享福祿。

translations.literal: Never has one without rites or reverence been able to enjoy blessings and emoluments for long.
translations.idiomatic: No one devoid of ritual and reverence has ever long enjoyed fortune and rank.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，不復周矣。

translations.literal: In my view, he will not complete another cycle."
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment, he will not last another full span."

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「若如卿言，則効在無遠，其子必復襲世，襲世之後，早晚當滅？

translations.literal: " The Shizu Emperor said: "If it is as you say, the effect is not far off; his son will surely inherit the succession—after that succession, how soon will he perish?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If you are right, the outcome is near; his son will surely succeed him—after that, how soon will the house fall?"

sentences.zh: 」順對曰：「臣略見其子，並非才俊，能保一隅。

translations.literal: " Shun replied: "I have briefly seen his sons; none are men of outstanding talent, able only to hold a corner of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun answered, "I have seen his sons briefly; none are gifted—they could hold only a corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 如聞敦煌太守牧犍，器性粗立，若繼蒙遜者必此人也。

translations.literal: As I hear, the Administrator of Dunhuang, Mujian, has a rough but established character; if anyone succeeds Mengxun, it must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Mujian, Administrator of Dunhuang, has a rough but forceful nature; if anyone succeeds Mengxun, it will be he.

sentences.zh: 然比之於父，僉云不逮。

translations.literal: Yet compared with his father, all say he does not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: Yet compared with his father, everyone agrees he falls short.

sentences.zh: 殆天所用資聖明也。

translations.literal: Perhaps Heaven uses this to supply Your Sagely Illumination."
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps Heaven means this to serve Your Sagely Illumination."

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「朕今方事于東，未暇營西，如卿所言，三五年間不足為晚。

translations.literal: " The Shizu Emperor said: "I am now engaged in affairs in the east and have no leisure to attend to the west; as you say, three to five years would not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I am occupied in the east and have no time for the west; as you say, three or five years would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 且停前計，以為後圖。

translations.literal: For now let us halt the earlier plan and keep it for a later design."
translations.idiomatic: For now we shall set aside the earlier plan and keep it for later."

sentences.zh: 」既而蒙遜死問至，世祖謂順曰：「卿言蒙遜死，今則驗矣，又言牧犍立，何其妙哉。

translations.literal: " Before long news of Mengxun's death arrived; the Shizu Emperor said to Shun: "You said Mengxun would die—now it is verified; you also said Mujian would succeed—how marvelous!"
translations.idiomatic: " Soon word of Mengxun's death arrived. The emperor said to Shun, "You said Mengxun would die—and so he has; you said Mujian would succeed—how remarkable!"

sentences.zh: 朕克涼州，亦當不遠。

translations.literal: My conquest of Liang Province should also be not far off."
translations.idiomatic: My conquest of Liang Province cannot be far away."

sentences.zh: 」於是賜絹千匹，廐馬一乘，進號安西將軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he bestowed a thousand bolts of silk, one imperial stable horse, and advanced his title to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave him a thousand bolts of silk, one horse from the imperial stables, and promoted him to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 寵待彌厚，政之巨細無所不參。

translations.literal: Favor and treatment grew still thicker; in affairs great and small he was consulted on all.
translations.idiomatic: His favor grew ever greater, and he was consulted on every matter of government, large or small.

sentences.zh: 崔浩惡之。

translations.literal: Cui Hao hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao detested him.

sentences.zh: 順凡使涼州十有二返，世祖稱其能。

translations.literal: Shun in all made twelve returns as envoy to Liang Province; the Shizu Emperor praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: In all Shun went twelve times as envoy to Liang Province, and the emperor praised his competence.

sentences.zh: 而蒙遜數與順遊宴，頗有悖慢之言，恐順東還泄之朝廷，尋以金寶納順懷中，故蒙遜罪釁得不聞徹。

translations.literal: Yet Mengxun several times feasted and toured with Shun and spoke words rather insolent and disrespectful; fearing that when Shun returned east he would reveal this to the court, he soon placed gold and treasures in Shun's bosom—thus Mengxun's offenses and faults did not reach full hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun often feasted and traveled with Shun and spoke with considerable insolence; fearing that Shun would report this when he returned east, he slipped gold and jewels into Shun's robes—so Mengxun's faults never reached the court in full.

sentences.zh: 浩知之，密言於世祖，世祖未之信。

translations.literal: Hao knew of this and spoke secretly to the Shizu Emperor, but the emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao learned of this and spoke privately to the emperor, who did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 太延三年，順復使涼州，及還，世祖曰：「昔與卿密圖，期之無遠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan, Shun was again sent to Liang Province; on his return the Shizu Emperor said: "Long ago I plotted with you in secret, expecting the day was not far.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiyan, Shun was sent to Liang Province again. On his return the emperor said, "Long ago you and I laid secret plans, expecting the day was near.

sentences.zh: 但以頃年東伐，未遑西顧，荏苒之間，遂及于此。

translations.literal: But because in recent years I campaigned eastward and had no leisure to look west, in the passing of time matters have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: But campaigns in the east left no time to look west, and in the passing years matters have come to this.

sentences.zh: 今和龍既平，三方無事，比繕甲治兵，指營河右，掃蕩萬里，今其時也。

translations.literal: Now Helong has been pacified and the three directions are without trouble; we are now repairing armor and training troops, aiming to operate west of the river and sweep clean ten thousand li—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Now Helong is pacified and the realm is quiet on three sides; we are repairing armor and drilling troops to march on the west of the river and sweep the land for ten thousand li—the time is now.

sentences.zh: 卿往復積歲，洞鑒廢興，若朕此年行師，當克以不？

translations.literal: You have gone back and forth for accumulated years and see clearly rise and fall—if I take the field this year, will I conquer or not?"
translations.idiomatic: You have traveled back and forth for years and know their rise and fall—if I campaign this year, will I succeed?"

sentences.zh: 」順對曰：「臣疇日所啟，私謂如然。

translations.literal: " Shun replied: "What I reported on other days I privately judged would be so.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun answered, "What I reported earlier I privately believed would prove true.

sentences.zh: 但民勞既久，未獲寧息，不可頻動，以增勞悴。

translations.literal: But the people have labored long and have not yet obtained rest and peace; we cannot move them frequently and add to their weariness and distress.
translations.idiomatic: But the people have labored long without rest; we must not stir them again and again and add to their exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 願待他年。

translations.literal: I wish to wait for another year."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we wait another year."

sentences.zh: 」世祖從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor Shizu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Shizu accepted it.

sentences.zh: 五年，議征涼州，順議以涼州乏水草，不宜遠征。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when a campaign against Liangzhou was debated, Shun argued that Liangzhou lacked grass and water and that a distant expedition was inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the court debated invading Liangzhou; Shun held that the region was short of fodder and water and that a long campaign should not be undertaken.

sentences.zh: 與崔浩庭諍。

translations.literal: He disputed the matter in open court with Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He and Cui Hao argued the point face to face before the throne.

sentences.zh: 浩固執以為宜征。

translations.literal: Hao stubbornly maintained that an expedition was proper.
translations.idiomatic: Hao held firm that the campaign should go forward.

sentences.zh: 世祖從浩議。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizu followed Hao's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sided with Hao.

sentences.zh: 及至姑臧，甚豐水草。

translations.literal: When they reached Guzang, grass and water proved very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Guzang they found pasture and water in great plenty.

sentences.zh: 世祖與恭宗書以言其事，頗銜順。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizu wrote to Crown Prince Gongzong about the matter and harbored considerable resentment toward Shun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote Crown Prince Gongzong to describe what had happened and nursed a strong grudge against Shun.

sentences.zh: 後謂浩曰：「卿昔所言，今果驗矣。

translations.literal: Later he said to Hao, "What you said before has now indeed been verified.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Hao, "What you told me then has come true.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「臣之所言，虛實皆如此類。

translations.literal: " Hao said, "What your servant has spoken, whether empty or solid, is all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao replied, "Everything I have told Your Majesty, whether it seemed doubtful or certain, turns out this way.

sentences.zh: 」初，蒙遜有西域沙門曇無讖，微有方術。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Mengxun had a monk from the Western Regions named Dharmarakṣa who possessed slight occult arts.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, among Mengxun's followers was the Western Regions monk Dharmarakṣa, who knew a little of esoteric arts.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔順令蒙遜送之京邑。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizu ordered Shun to have Mengxun send him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu instructed Shun to have Mengxun escort the monk to the capital.

sentences.zh: 順受蒙遜金，聽其殺之。

translations.literal: Shun accepted gold from Mengxun and allowed him to kill the monk.
translations.idiomatic: Shun took a bribe from Mengxun and let him have the monk put to death.

sentences.zh: 世祖克涼州後，聞而嫌順。

translations.literal: After the Emperor Shizu conquered Liangzhou, he heard of this and came to dislike Shun.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took Liangzhou and learned of it, his distaste for Shun deepened.

sentences.zh: 涼土既平，詔順差次羣臣，賜以爵位。

translations.literal: Once the Liang region was pacified, an edict charged Shun with ranking the officials and bestowing ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang lands were pacified, Shun was ordered to rank the officials and assign them titles and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 順頗受納，品第不平。

translations.literal: Shun accepted many bribes, and his gradings were not fair.
translations.idiomatic: Shun took substantial bribes and graded men unfairly.

sentences.zh: 涼州人徐桀發其事。

translations.literal: A man of Liangzhou named Xu Jie exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie of Liangzhou brought the matter to light.

sentences.zh: 浩又毀之，云：「順昔受牧犍父子重賂，每言涼州無水草，不可行師。

translations.literal: Hao again slandered him, saying, "Shun formerly received heavy bribes from Mujian and his father and always said that Liangzhou had no grass or water and that troops could not march there.
translations.idiomatic: Hao attacked him again, saying, "Shun once took lavish gifts from Juqu Mujian and his father and kept insisting Liangzhou lacked fodder and water and that an army could not be sent.

sentences.zh: 及陛下至姑臧，水草豐足。

translations.literal: Yet when Your Majesty reached Guzang, grass and water were plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Your Majesty reached Guzang, pasture and water were abundant.

sentences.zh: 其詐如此，幾誤國事。

translations.literal: His deceit was of this sort and nearly ruined the state's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His fraud was so brazen that it nearly wrecked the campaign.

sentences.zh: 不忠若是，反言臣讒之於陛下。

translations.literal: Disloyal to this degree, he in turn says that your servant slandered him before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: So disloyal, yet he turns around and claims that I maligned him to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」世祖大怒，真君三年遂刑順於城西。

translations.literal: " The Emperor Shizu was greatly enraged, and in the third year of Zhenjun he executed Shun west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Shizu flew into a rage and, in the third year of Zhenjun, had Shun executed west of the capital.

sentences.zh: 順死後數年，其從父弟孝伯為世祖知重，居中用事。

translations.literal: Several years after Shun's death, his paternal cousin Xiaobo came to be valued by Emperor Shizu and held power at court.
translations.idiomatic: A few years after Shun died, his cousin Xiaobo won the emperor's trust and wielded authority at the center of government.

sentences.zh: 及浩之誅，世祖怒甚，謂孝伯曰：「卿從兄往雖誤國，朕意亦未便至此。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed, the Emperor Shizu was very angry and said to Xiaobo, "Your elder cousin did harm the state in the past, yet my mind was not yet inclined to go so far as this.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was put to death, Emperor Shizu was furious and told Xiaobo, "Your cousin once misled the state, but I had not meant to go this far.

sentences.zh: 由浩譖毀，朕忿遂盛。

translations.literal: Because of Hao's slander and defamation, my wrath then grew intense.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's slanders stoked my anger until it boiled over.

sentences.zh: 殺卿從兄者，浩也。

translations.literal: The one who killed your elder cousin was Hao.
translations.idiomatic: It was Hao who brought about your cousin's death.

sentences.zh: 」皇興初，順子敷等貴寵，顯祖追贈順侍中、鎮西大將軍、太尉公、高平王，諡曰宣王，妻邢氏曰孝妃。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Huangxing, Shun's son Fu and others were honored and favored; Emperor Xianzu posthumously enfeoffed Shun as Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Commandant, and Prince of Gaoping, with the posthumous title Prince Xuan; his wife, the Xing clan, was styled Consort Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: " Early in Huangxing, Fu and the other sons rose to favor; Emperor Xianzu posthumously made Shun Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Commandant, and Prince of Gaoping, posthumous name Prince Xuan, and styled his wife Lady Xing Consort Xiao.

sentences.zh: 順四子。

translations.literal: Shun had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shun had four sons.

sentences.zh: 長子敷，字景文。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Fu, courtesy name Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Fu, was styled Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 真君二年，選入中書教學。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenjun he was selected for instruction in the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenjun he was chosen for training in the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以忠謹給侍東宮。

translations.literal: Because of his loyalty and prudence he was assigned to attend the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty and discretion won him a post attending the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 又為中散，與李訢、盧遐、度世等並以聰敏內參機密，出入詔命。

translations.literal: He also served as Palace Scribe and, together with Li Xin, Lu Xia, Dushi, and others, by his intelligence took part in confidential affairs within and drafted edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as palace scribe; with Li Xin, Lu Xia, Dushi, and others he was counted among the sharp minds who handled secret business and drafted imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 敷性謙恭，加有文學，高宗寵遇之。

translations.literal: Fu was by nature modest and respectful, and moreover possessed literary learning; Emperor Gaozong favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was humble and well read, and Emperor Gaozong showered him with favor.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書下大夫，典掌要切，加前軍將軍，賜爵平棘子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Grand Master of the Secretariat, in charge of urgent matters, and additionally made General of the Van, with enfeoffment as Marquis of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to junior grand master of the Secretariat in charge of pressing affairs, was made General of the Van, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 後兼錄南部，遷散騎常侍、南部尚書、中書監，領內外祕書。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently supervised the Southern Department, was promoted to Attendant Cavalier, Southern Department Director, and Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, and oversaw internal and external secretarial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also oversaw the Southern Department, then became attendant cavalier, southern director, and supervisor of the Central Secretariat, heading both inner and outer secretarial work.

sentences.zh: 襲爵高平公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the dukedom of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 朝政大議，事無不關。

translations.literal: In great deliberations of court government, there was no matter in which he was not involved.
translations.idiomatic: No major policy debate passed without his involvement.

sentences.zh: 及劉彧徐州刺史薛安都、司州刺史常珍奇以彭城、懸瓠降附，于時朝議，謂彼誠偽未可信保。

translations.literal: When Xue Andu, regional inspector of Xuzhou under Liu Yu, and Chang Zhenqi, regional inspector of Sizhou, surrendered Pengcheng and Xuanchi, at that time court opinion held that their sincerity or falsity could not yet be trusted and relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Andu, Liu Song's inspector of Xuzhou, and Chang Zhenqi, inspector of Sizhou, surrendered Pengcheng and Xuanchi, the court doubted whether their submission was genuine.

sentences.zh: 敷乃固執必然，曰：「劉氏喪亂，釁起蕭牆，骨肉內離，藩屏外叛。

translations.literal: Fu then stubbornly insisted it was certain and said, "The Liu house is in disorder; trouble arises within the palace walls; kin turn against one another within, and the border screens rebel without.
translations.idiomatic: Fu held firm that the moment was ripe and said, "The Liu regime is collapsing: strife has broken out at court, kin are tearing one another apart, and the frontier lords are defecting.

sentences.zh: 今以皇朝之靈，兵馬之力，兼并之會，宜在於今。

translations.literal: Now, with the numinous power of the imperial house and the strength of arms and horses, the occasion for annexation ought to be seized today.
translations.idiomatic: With the dynasty's mandate and our armies at full strength, the chance to conquer belongs to this moment.

sentences.zh: 況安都、珍奇識機歸命，奉誠萬里，小民元元，企仰皇化。

translations.literal: Moreover, Andu and Zhenqi recognized the moment and submitted; they offer loyalty from ten thousand li away, and the common people in their masses look up in hope to imperial transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Andu and Zhenqi have read the times and come over in good faith from afar; the common folk are yearning for our rule.

sentences.zh: 今之事機，安可復失？

translations.literal: How can the opportunity of the present moment be allowed to slip away again?
translations.idiomatic: How can we let this chance slip by?

sentences.zh: 」於是眾議乃同，遣師接援。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the assembled opinion agreed, and troops were dispatched to receive and support them.
translations.idiomatic: " The court fell in line and sent armies to accept and reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 淮海寧輯，敷有力焉。

translations.literal: When the Huai and sea regions were pacified and put in order, Fu had a strong hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai-Hai region was brought to peace in no small part through Fu's efforts.

sentences.zh: 敷既見待二世，兄弟親戚在朝者十有餘人。

translations.literal: Fu had been favored through two reigns, and brothers and kinsmen holding office at court numbered more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had enjoyed favor under two emperors, and more than a dozen brothers and relatives held posts at court.

sentences.zh: 弟弈又有寵於文明太后。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi was also favored by Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yi likewise enjoyed the empress dowager's favor.

sentences.zh: 李訢列其隱罪二十餘條，顯祖大怒，皇興四年冬，誅敷兄弟，削順位號為庶人。

translations.literal: Li Xin listed more than twenty hidden offenses; Emperor Xianzu was greatly enraged, and in the winter of the fourth year of Huangxing he executed Fu and his brothers and reduced Shun's rank and title to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin laid out more than twenty concealed crimes; Emperor Xianzu was furious, and in the winter of Huangxing year four he executed Fu and his brothers and stripped Shun's house of its noble rank.

sentences.zh: 敷從弟顯德、妹夫廣平宋叔珍等，皆坐關亂公私，同時伏法。

translations.literal: Fu's younger cousin Xiande, his sister's husband Song Shuzhen of Guangping, and others were all convicted of meddling in and disturbing public and private affairs and were executed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's cousin Xiande, his brother-in-law Song Shuzhen of Guangping, and others were all convicted of abusing public office for private ends and were executed together.

sentences.zh: 敷兄弟敦崇孝義，家門有禮，至於居喪法度，吉凶書記，皆合典則，為北州所稱美。

translations.literal: Fu and his brothers were earnest in honoring filial piety and righteousness; the household observed ritual propriety, and in mourning rites, auspicious and inauspicious correspondence, all accorded with canonical norms and were praised throughout the northern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu brothers were devoted to filial duty and decorum; their household rituals for mourning and for letters of congratulation or condolence all met canonical standards and won praise across the north.

sentences.zh: 既致斯禍，時人歎惜之。

translations.literal: Once they met this calamity, people of the time sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck, contemporaries mourned what they had lost.

sentences.zh: 敷長子伯和。

translations.literal: Fu's eldest son was Bohe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's eldest son was Bohe.

sentences.zh: 次仲良，與父俱死。

translations.literal: The next, Zhongliang, died together with his father.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Zhongliang, died with his father.

sentences.zh: 伯和走竄歲餘，為人執送，殺之。

translations.literal: Bohe fled and hid for more than a year, was seized and sent in by others, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bohe was on the run for more than a year before he was captured and handed over, then executed.

sentences.zh: 伯和有庶子孝祖，年小藏免。

translations.literal: Bohe had a son by a concubine, Xiaozu, who was young and was hidden away and spared.
translations.idiomatic: Bohe had a concubine-born son, Xiaozu, who was still a child and was hidden away to escape death.

sentences.zh: 後敷妻崔氏得出宮，養之。

translations.literal: Later Fu's wife, the Cui clan, was able to leave the palace and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fu's wife, Lady Cui, was released from the palace and raised the boy.

sentences.zh: 至平涼太守。

translations.literal: He rose to become Administrator of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became administrator of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 敷弟式，字景則。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother was Shi, courtesy name Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Shi was styled Jingze.

sentences.zh: 學業知名。

translations.literal: He was renowned for his scholarly attainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 歷散騎常侍、平東將軍、西兗州刺史，濮陽侯。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Attendant Cavalier, General Who Pacifies the East, and Regional Inspector of Western Yanzhou, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant cavalier, general who pacifies the east, and regional inspector of Western Yanzhou, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 式自以家據權要，心慮危禍，常敕津吏；

translations.literal: Shi, considering that his family held power at the center, feared disaster in his heart and constantly instructed the ferry officials:
translations.idiomatic: Shi knew his clan sat at the heart of power and lived in fear of ruin, so he constantly told the ferry guards:

sentences.zh: 臺有使者，必先啟告，然後渡之。

translations.literal: "If the capital sends envoys, you must first report to me, and only then allow them to cross."
translations.idiomatic: "If envoys come from the capital, report to me before you let them cross."

sentences.zh: 既而使人平曉卒至，津吏欲先告式，使者紿云：「我須南過，不停此州，不煩令刺史知也。

translations.literal: Before long an envoy named Ping Xiao arrived suddenly; the ferry official wished to report first to Shi, but the envoy deceived him, saying, "I must pass south and will not stop in this province; there is no need to trouble the regional inspector to know.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an envoy named Ping Xiao arrived without warning; the ferry guard started to notify Shi, but the envoy lied, "I am only passing south and will not linger in your province—no need to trouble your inspector.

sentences.zh: 」津人信之，與使俱渡。

translations.literal: " The ferryman believed him and crossed together with the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: " The ferryman believed him and let him cross with the envoy.

sentences.zh: 使者既濟，突入執式赴都，與兄俱死。

translations.literal: Once the envoy had crossed, he burst in, seized Shi, and took him to the capital; he died together with his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: After the crossing the envoy stormed in, seized Shi, and hauled him to the capital, where he was executed alongside his brother.

sentences.zh: 式子憲，字仲軌。

translations.literal: Shi's son was Xian, courtesy name Zhonggui.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's son Xian was styled Zhonggui.

sentences.zh: 清粹，善風儀，好學，有器度。

translations.literal: He was pure and refined, skilled in bearing and deportment, fond of learning, and possessed breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: He was refined in manner, graceful in bearing, eager to learn, and broad-minded.

sentences.zh: 太和初，襲爵，又降為伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he inherited the title, which was then reduced to that of marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he inherited the family title, which was soon reduced to a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 拜祕書中散，雅為高祖所賞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Scribe and was greatly admired by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace scribe and won Emperor Gaozu's high regard.

sentences.zh: 稍遷散騎侍郎，接對蕭衍使蕭琛、范雲。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Gentleman Attendant Cavalier and received and answered the envoys of Xiao Yan, Xiao Chen and Fan Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman attendant cavalier and received Liang envoys from Xiao Yan, including Xiao Chen and Fan Yun.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞歸養，拜趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he begged to return home to support her and was appointed Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to care for his aging mother and was appointed administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 趙脩與其州里，脩歸葬父母也，牧守以下畏之累跡，惟憲不為之屈，時人高之。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiu was from the same commandery; Xiu had returned to bury his parents, and prefects and inspectors below all feared him and crowded in his train, but only Xian would not bow to him, and people of the time held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu, a fellow townsman who had come home to bury his parents, had every local official scurrying to pay court—only Xian refused to bend, and contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 轉授驍騎將軍、尚書左丞、長兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, and Senior Concurrent Master of Writing in the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of valiant cavalry, left assistant director of the Masters of Writing, and senior concurrent personnel director.

sentences.zh: 遷長兼司徒左長史、定州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Senior Concurrent Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and Senior Rectifier of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became senior concurrent left chief clerk of the Ministry of Education and senior rectifier of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋遷河南尹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 參議新令於尚書上省。

translations.literal: He took part in deliberating the new statutes at the upper offices of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He helped draft the new statutes in the upper secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永平三年，出為左將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongping he went out as General of the Left and Regional Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping year three he was sent out as general of the left and regional inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，坐事除名。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because of an offense he was struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後以黨附高肇，為御史所劾。

translations.literal: Later, because he had attached himself to the faction of Gao Zhao, he was impeached by the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was impeached by the censorate for siding with Gao Zhao's faction.

sentences.zh: 事具高聰傳。

translations.literal: The affair is given in full in the biography of Gao Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Gao Cong.

sentences.zh: 正光二年二月，肅宗講於國子堂，召憲預聽，又以子騫為國子生。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhenguang, Emperor Suzong lectured in the Hall of the Imperial Academy; Xian was summoned to attend and listen, and his son Qian was also made a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhenguang year two Emperor Suzong lectured at the Imperial Academy; Xian was invited to attend, and his son Qian was enrolled as a student.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜光祿大夫，復本爵濮陽伯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and restored to his original enfeoffment as Marquis of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made grand master of splendid happiness and restored to his marquisate of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，除持節、安西將軍、行雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, and Acting Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the west, and acting regional inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋除七兵尚書，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Director of the Seven Armies in the Masters of Writing and additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made director of the seven armies and additionally general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，元法僧據徐州反叛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Yuan Faseng seized Xuzhou and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang Yuan Faseng seized Xuzhou and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔憲為使持節、假鎮東將軍、徐州都督，與安豐王延明、臨淮王彧等討之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xian as Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Pacifies the East, and Area Commander of Xuzhou, to campaign against him together with the Prince of Anfeng Yanming, the Prince of Linhuai Yu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was ordered out as bearer of the staff, acting general who pacifies the east, and area commander of Xuzhou, to join the Prince of Anfeng Yanming, the Prince of Linhuai Yu, and others in suppressing the revolt.

sentences.zh: 會蕭衍遣其豫章王綜據彭城，俄而綜降。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang Zong to hold Pengcheng, and before long Zong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xiao Yan sent his Prince of Yuzhang to hold Pengcheng, and Zong soon surrendered.

sentences.zh: 徐州既平，詔遣兼黃門侍郎常景詣軍慰勞，賜憲驊騮馬一匹，仍除征東將軍、揚州刺史、淮南大都督。

translations.literal: Once Xuzhou was pacified, an edict sent Concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Chang Jing to the army to offer comfort and rewards; Xian was granted one piebald stallion and was then appointed General Who Campaigns East, Regional Inspector of Yangzhou, and Grand Area Commander of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuzhou was secured, the court sent attendant Chang Jing to reward the troops, gave Xian a piebald stallion, and appointed him general who campaigns east, regional inspector of Yangzhou, and grand area commander of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 二年，蕭衍遣其平北將軍元樹、右衞將軍胡龍牙、護軍將軍夏侯亶等來寇壽陽。

translations.literal: In the second year, Xiao Yan sent his General Who Pacifies the North Yuan Shu, General of the Right Guard Hu Longya, General Who Protects the Army Xiahou Dan, and others to invade Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Xiao Yan sent his general who pacifies the north Yuan Shu, general of the right guard Hu Longya, general who protects the army Xiahou Dan, and others against Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 樹等從下蔡軍於城之東北，亶從黎漿而屯於城南。

translations.literal: Shu and the others advanced from Xiaxia and encamped northeast of the city; Dan came from Lijiang and stationed his forces south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's force marched from Xiaxia and camped northeast of the city, while Dan advanced from Lijiang and took position to the south.

sentences.zh: 憲謂不先破元樹等，則夏侯亶無由可克，乃遣子長鈞率眾逆戰。

translations.literal: Xian said that unless Yuan Shu and the others were first broken, there would be no way to overcome Xiahou Dan, and he therefore sent his son Changjun at the head of the host to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xian reasoned that Dan could not be beaten until Shu was defeated, and sent his son Changjun out to give battle.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，長鈞見執。

translations.literal: The army was defeated and Changjun was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The army was beaten and Changjun taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 樹等乘之，憲力屈，以城降。

translations.literal: Shu and the others pressed the advantage; Xian's strength was exhausted, and he surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shu pressed the attack; with his strength spent, Xian surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 因求還國，衍聽歸。

translations.literal: He then begged to return to his state, and Yan permitted him to go home.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return to Wei, and Xiao Yan let him go.

sentences.zh: 既至，敕付廷尉。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, an edict handed him over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On his return an edict turned him over to the minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，憲女壻安樂王鑒據相州反。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, Xian's son-in-law, Prince Anle Jian, seized Xiangzhou and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in the third year Xian's son-in-law, Prince Anle Jian, seized Xiangzhou and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 靈太后謂鑒心懷劫脅，遂詔賜憲死，時年五十八。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling said that Jian harbored thoughts of holding others hostage by force, and an edict then ordered Xian to be granted death; he was fifty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling believed Jian had coerced Xian into the revolt and ordered Xian put to death; he was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，贈使持節、侍中、都督定冀相殷四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書令、定州刺史，諡曰文靜。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was posthumously granted the titles Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Area Commander of the Military Affairs of the Four Provinces Ding, Ji, Xiang, and Yin, General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi he was posthumously made bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of the four provinces Ding, Ji, Xiang, and Yin, general of agile cavalry with honors equal to the three dukes, director of the Masters of Writing, and regional inspector of Dingzhou, posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 子希遠，字景冲。

translations.literal: His son was Xiyuan, courtesy name Jingchong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiyuan was styled Jingchong.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 子祖悛，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Zujuan inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zujuan inherited the family title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced as usual.

sentences.zh: 希遠兄長鈞，興和中，梁州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: Xiyuan's elder brother Jun, in the Xinghe era, was Chief Clerk of the Liang Province Rapid Cavalry Commandery Office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan's elder brother Jun served as chief clerk of the Liang Province Rapid Cavalry headquarters during the Xinghe period.

sentences.zh: 希遠第二弟希宗，字景玄。

translations.literal: Xiyuan's second younger brother was Xizong, styled Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: His second younger brother was Xizong, styled Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 出後憲兄。

translations.literal: He was made heir to his elder brother Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted as heir to his elder brother Xian.

sentences.zh: 性寬和，儀貌雅麗，涉獵書傳，有文才。

translations.literal: By nature he was gentle and harmonious, of elegant and handsome appearance, broadly versed in canonical texts and histories, and possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle by nature, handsome and refined in bearing, widely read in the classics and histories, and gifted as a writer.

sentences.zh: 起家太尉參軍事，轉直後，領侍御史，遷通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He began his career as an aide in the Ministry of the Imperial Secretariat, transferred to Attendant Behind, served as supervising censor, and was promoted to Cadet Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a secretariat aide, became an imperial attendant in the rear guard, then supervising censor, and rose to cadet regular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋為東南道行臺邸珍右丞，與諸軍討賊於彭沛，克之，轉齊獻武王大行臺郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was right deputy of the Southeastern Circuit Mobile Commandery under Di Zhen; with the various armies he campaigned against bandits in Peng and Pei, defeated them, and was transferred to senior clerk in Grand Duke Xianwu of Qi's mobile commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became right deputy on the southeastern mobile staff under Di Zhen, joined the armies in suppressing bandits in Peng and Pei, took them, and was transferred to senior clerk on Prince Xianwu of Qi's mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、中軍大將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Central Army, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Emblem.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regular palace attendant, grand general of the central army, and grand master of splendid happiness with the golden emblem.

sentences.zh: 獻武王擢為中外府長史，為齊王納其第二女。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi promoted him to chief administrator of the Central and Foreign Affairs Office, and the Prince of Qi took his second daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi made him chief administrator of the central and foreign affairs office, and the prince took his second daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 希宗以人望兼美，深見禮遇。

translations.literal: Because Xizong combined popular esteem with excellence, he was deeply honored.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong united public regard with personal merit and was treated with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 出行上黨太守。

translations.literal: He went out on assignment as Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 尋而遘疾，興和二年四月卒於郡，年四十。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; in the fourth month of the second year of Xinghe he died in the prefecture at age forty.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died in the prefecture in the fourth month of the second year of Xinghe, at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、都督定冀滄瀛殷五州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司空公、殷州刺史，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for the Five Provinces of Ding, Ji, Cang, Ying, and Yin, Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief, Duke of Works, and Governor of Yin Province, with the posthumous epithet Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief over military affairs in Ding, Ji, Cang, Ying, and Yin, rapid cavalry general-in-chief, duke of works, and governor of Yin, with the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 長子祖昇，武定末，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zusheng, at the end of the Wuding era, was Washing Horse of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zusheng, late in the Wuding period, served as washing horse to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 希宗弟希仁，字景山。

translations.literal: Xizong's younger brother was Xiren, styled Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong's younger brother Xiren was styled Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 武定末，國子祭酒、兼給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era he was Chancellor of the National University and concurrently Supervising Secretariat Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuding he was chancellor of the national university and concurrently supervising gentleman of the yellow gate in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 希仁弟騫，字希義。

translations.literal: Xiren's younger brother was Qian, styled Xiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiren's younger brother Qian was styled Xiyi.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，文藻富盛。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics and histories, and rich in literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged widely through the classics and histories, and his writing was lush with ornament.

sentences.zh: 年十四，國子學生。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was a student of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he enrolled as a student of the national university.

sentences.zh: 以聰達見知。

translations.literal: He was known for his intelligence and quickness.
translations.idiomatic: He won notice for his keen intelligence.

sentences.zh: 歷大將軍府法曹參軍、太宰府主簿，轉中散大夫，遷中書舍人，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He successively served as legal affairs aide in the Grand General's office and chief clerk in the Grand Preceptor's office, transferred to Palace Cadet, was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, and was given the added title of Cadet Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as legal aide in the grand general's office and chief clerk in the grand preceptor's office, became a palace cadet, rose to secretariat gentleman, and was given the added rank of cadet regular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 曾為釋情賦，曰：

translations.literal: He once composed a "Rhapsody on Releasing Emotions," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a Rhapsody on Releasing Emotions, which runs:

sentences.zh: 單閼之年，無射之月，余承乏攝官，直於本省。

translations.literal: In the year of Shanjian, in the month of Wuyi, I hold an inadequate acting appointment and am on duty at the imperial secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of Shanjian, in the month of Wuyi, I hold a modest acting post on rotation within the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 對九重之清切，望八襲之崢嶸，感代序以長懷，觀爽氣而軫慮。

translations.literal: Facing the pure solemnity of the ninefold palace, gazing at the lofty mass of the eightfold ramparts, I am stirred by the succession of seasons to long reflections, and viewing the clear autumn air turn my thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court's chill clarity and beneath the towering eightfold walls, the turning seasons stir long reflection, and the crisp air turns my mind inward.

sentences.zh: 籠樊之念既多，寥廓之想彌切。

translations.literal: Thoughts of the cage and barrier are many; yearning for open space grows keener.
translations.idiomatic: The urge to flee confinement grows ever stronger; the longing for wide horizons deepens.

sentences.zh: 含毫有思，斐然成賦。

translations.literal: Holding the brush with thought, I have shaped this fu in splendid form.
translations.idiomatic: Brush in hand, intent gathered—I have wrought this fu into shining lines.

sentences.zh: 猶潘生之秋興，王子之登閣也。

translations.literal: It is like Pan Yue's autumn meditation or Wang Can's ascent to the tower.
translations.idiomatic: As Pan Yue wrote when autumn stirred him, as Wang Can wrote upon climbing the storied pavilion.

sentences.zh: 厠鄭璞於周寶，編魚目於隨珠，未敢自同作者，蓋亦各言爾志云。

translations.literal: I rank a Zheng stone beside Zhou's treasure and thread fish eyes among Sui pearls; I dare not rank myself with the masters—yet each may speak his own aim.
translations.idiomatic: I set a rough Zheng jade beside Zhou's regalia and string fish eyes with Sui pearls; I dare not call myself their peer—yet each man may speak what moves him.

sentences.zh: 荷峻極之層構，導積石之洪流。

translations.literal: Bearing the layered structures of highest peak, channeling the mighty torrent of heaped stone.
translations.idiomatic: Upheld by the tiered height of the Sacred Peak, fed by the piled-stone torrent's flow.

sentences.zh: 有馬形而謨舜，亦龍德而史周。

translations.literal: There was horse shape and Shun was counseled; there was dragon virtue and the Zhou was chronicled.
translations.idiomatic: The horse-shaped omen counseled Shun; dragon virtue filled the Zhou Annals.

sentences.zh: 爰相趙之鴻烈，逮藩魏之優遊。

translations.literal: Then followed Zhao's great splendor, reaching the easy leisure of the Wei fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus arose Zhao's great blaze of glory, down to the ease of Wei as a feudal house.

sentences.zh: 為衢樽於上葉，號木鐸於前修。

translations.literal: A crossroads wine-jar for the upper age, a wooden clapper bell for the former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: For the former age a wine-jar stood at the crossroads; for past worthies the wooden bell was rung.

sentences.zh: 若豢龍之不隕，似窮桑之世濟。

translations.literal: Like raising dragons unperishing, as Kuangsang sustained the world through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Like dragon-tenders who never fell, like Kuangsang's line sustaining age after age.

sentences.zh: [1]故抱玉而懷珠，且滋蘭而樹蕙。

translations.literal: [1] Thus embracing jade and cherishing pearls, both nourishing orchids and planting spices.
translations.idiomatic: [1] So they clasped jade and treasured pearls, and grew orchids while planting sweet herbs.

sentences.zh: 或舟楫以匡時，或棲遲以卒歲。

translations.literal: Some by boat and oar steadied the age; some lingered in retreat to end their years.
translations.idiomatic: Some took boat and oar to right the times; some dwelt in seclusion until life's close.

sentences.zh: 尚無忝於先人，諒貽厥於來裔。

translations.literal: Still without shame before their forebears, assuredly bequeathing merit to coming generations.
translations.idiomatic: None failed their ancestors; all left blessing for those who followed.

sentences.zh: 書金冊以葳蕤，布銀繩而昭晣。

translations.literal: Inscribed gold registers lush and profuse, spread silver cords shining clear.
translations.idiomatic: Gold tablets bloomed with flourish; silver cords gleamed bright.

sentences.zh: 清風忽其緬邈，啟皇祖於庚寅。

translations.literal: The pure wind suddenly receded far away; the founding ancestor rose in the gengyin year.
translations.idiomatic: Then the clear wind vanished into distance; our founding forebear rose in the year gengyin.

sentences.zh: 〈李伯仁上東門銘曰：「上東少陽，厥位在寅。

translations.literal: (Li Boren's inscription on the Upper East Gate says: "Upper East is lesser yang; its position lies in yin.
translations.idiomatic: (In Li Boren's Inscription on the Upper East Gate: "Upper East is minor yang, its seat in yin.

sentences.zh: 條風動物，月值孟春。

translations.literal: The gentle spring wind stirs all things; the month falls in early spring.
translations.idiomatic: The early wind stirs the creatures; the month stands at spring's first fullness.

sentences.zh: 」王武子詩曰：「於顯我王，緝乘斯民。

translations.literal: " Wang Wuzi's poem says: "How glorious our king, steering this people.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Wuzi's poem runs: "How glorious our king, gathering this people.

sentences.zh: 俊明有德，嚴恭惟夤。」〉

translations.literal: Wise and bright and virtuous, stern and reverent in service.")
translations.idiomatic: Wise, bright, and virtuous, stern and reverent in duty.")

sentences.zh: 逢軒教之方洽，遇周命之惟新。

translations.literal: When Xuanyuan's teaching was in full concord, one met the Zhou mandate made anew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Emperor's teaching spread in harmony, one met the Zhou mandate born anew.

sentences.zh: 譬龍虎其有合，信山川而降神。

translations.literal: As dragon and tiger gather in concord, truly mountains and rivers sent down the divine.
translations.idiomatic: When dragon met tiger in kinship, river and hill sent down the sacred.

sentences.zh: 若勝庭之五傑，似不速之三人。

translations.literal: Like the five worthies of the Winning Court, like the three men of unhurried coming.
translations.idiomatic: As the five heroes of the Winning Court, as the three men who came without being summoned.

sentences.zh: 協嗜欲於將至，豈物色而方臻。

translations.literal: Desires harmonized before arrival—how could one seek them out only when talent appeared?
translations.idiomatic: Hearts matched before they came near—never merely scouting for gifts once gifts were in view.

sentences.zh: 荷天寵以來儀，步康衢而騁力。

translations.literal: Bearing heaven's favor they came to serve, treading the smooth highway and exerting their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Laden with heaven's grace they came to court; on the broad road they strained their powers.

sentences.zh: 如乾元之利貞，若坤四之方直。

translations.literal: Like Qian's solid good fortune, like Kun's fourth line's square straightness.
translations.idiomatic: As Qian's firm profit and rectitude, as the fourth Kun line's square and straight.

sentences.zh: 內弼諧於本朝，外闢土於殊域。

translations.literal: Within they harmonized the native dynasty; without they opened territory in distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: Within, allies to the throne's house; without, captains who broke ground in foreign realms.

sentences.zh: 乘紫氛以厲羽，負青天而鼓翼。

translations.literal: Riding purple mist they sharpened their pinions; bearing the blue sky they beat their wings.
translations.idiomatic: They breasted purple haze to harden their wings and shouldered the azure sky to drum the air.

sentences.zh: 既公侯之必復，亦慶緒之所融。

translations.literal: As marquis and duke must return, so too the auspicious lineage they folded together.
translations.idiomatic: What marquis and duke must regain, the house's blessed thread likewise braided.

sentences.zh: 績並樹於八凱，道俱升於二宮。

translations.literal: Merits planted together with the Eight Worthies; the Way climbed with them to both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds stood beside the Eight Worthies; the Way rose with them to both halls.

sentences.zh: 遂遵流以至海，且因岳而為嵩。

translations.literal: Then followed the stream till it reached the sea; took the mountain for Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: They followed the current to the sea and took the lesser hill for sacred Song.

sentences.zh: 同羽儀於班氏，均載德於楊公。

translations.literal: Feathers and standards like the Ban clan; virtue borne together like the Yang house.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Ban house in court regalia, like the Yang clan in bearing virtue.

sentences.zh: 何日月之逾邁，引寒暑而相終。

translations.literal: How the sun and moon hasten away; they draw cold and heat to mutual close.
translations.idiomatic: How sun and moon hurry on, drawing cold and heat each to its term.

sentences.zh: 委晉會於弱齒，遺堂構於微躬。

translations.literal: He entrusted the Jin court to my tender years; left the great hall-frame to my slight person.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he handed me the Jin succession; to my frail frame he left the ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 嗟蒙昧之無取，故告舍而不及。

translations.literal: Alas—ignorant, nothing to take; therefore the farewell speech never caught me.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, in stupidity I had nothing he could claim; his parting words never reached me in time.

sentences.zh: 已濩落而少成，又擁腫而無立。

translations.literal: Already scattered and fallen with slight success, again swollen and stunted without standing.
translations.idiomatic: Already cast loose with small attainment, and swollen, twisted, with nothing to uphold.

sentences.zh: 愧精堅於百鍊，慚忠信於十邑。

translations.literal: Ashamed before steel refined a hundred times, shamed before loyalty and faith across ten towns.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed beside iron tempered a hundredfold, ashamed beside faith kept through ten domains.

sentences.zh: 非珪璋之特達，詎芳菲之易襲。

translations.literal: Not jade-scepter's special penetration—how could fragrant bloom be lightly seized?
translations.idiomatic: No jade tablet's rare clarity—how dare one lightly wear fame's blossom?

sentences.zh: 未砥礪以自進，寧琢磨而成章。

translations.literal: Not yet sharpening myself to advance—would I rather polish and polish till the piece is formed?
translations.idiomatic: Not yet whetting myself toward advance—would I polish on until a chapter forms?

sentences.zh: 乖宋子之萬字，異應生之五行。

translations.literal: Unlike Songzi's ten thousand characters, unlike Yingsheng's five shifts.
translations.idiomatic: No match for Song son's ten thousand graphs, nor for Ying's birth of the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 不請觀於石室，豈借書於晉皇。

translations.literal: Not asking to view the stone chamber, not borrowing books from the Jin emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Not seeking to view the Stone Chamber, not borrowing books from Jin's throne.

sentences.zh: 求班莊而不遂，[2]況蔡文之可望？

translations.literal: Seeking Ban and Zhuang yet not attaining, [2] how much less can Cai Wen be hoped for?
translations.idiomatic: I sought Ban and the Kangs and did not win them; [2] how then Cai Yong's vision?

sentences.zh: 參四科其未獲，入三選而誰許。

translations.literal: Not attaining the four categories, entering the three selections—who would grant it?
translations.idiomatic: The four ranks I never secured; who would admit me to the three lists?

sentences.zh: 本無聲於梁魏，故未聞於陳汝。

translations.literal: Fundamentally without fame in Liang and Wei, therefore unheard of in Chen and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: From the first unknown in Liang and Wei, and so unheard in Chen and Ru.

sentences.zh: 居玉石以多迷，宅顯晦而乖所。

translations.literal: Dwelling amid jade and stone yet much bewildered, lodging in fame and obscurity yet wrong in place.
translations.idiomatic: Amid jade and pebbles I lose my way; in glare and shadow I miss my place.

sentences.zh: 既無懷於四至，安有情於再舉。

translations.literal: Since without thought of the four extremities, how could there be feeling for rising twice?
translations.idiomatic: With no heart for the four quarters, what zeal could I have to rise again?

sentences.zh: 雖衣冠之末冑，而世祿之緒餘。
