translations.literal: Though the trailing fringe of cap and robe, yet a thread of age-long salary.
translations.idiomatic: Though last rank in gown and cap, still a thread of hereditary stipend.

sentences.zh: 等渤澥之乘雁，類九罭之逃魚。

translations.literal: Equal to riding the goose on the Bo Sea, similar to fish escaping the nine-fold net.
translations.idiomatic: Like the goose crossing the Bo Sea, like fish slipping the ninefold net.

sentences.zh: 處江淮而不變，對朝市而閑居。

translations.literal: Dwelling on Jiang and Huai unchanged, facing court and market in idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huai and Yang I stay unchanged; before court and mart I dwell at ease.

sentences.zh: 空闔門以靖軌，非論道而修書。

translations.literal: Empty—closing the gate in quiet tracks, not discussing the Way but studying books.
translations.idiomatic: The gates shut on a quiet path; I do not preach the Way but mend my books.

sentences.zh: 少賓客於季彥，謝朋交於太初。

translations.literal: Few guests like Jiyan's circle, farewell to friends like Taichu's day.
translations.idiomatic: Few guests as in Jiyan's time; old companions gone as at Taichu's parting.

sentences.zh: 在正光之御曆，實明皇之拱己。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang reign he held the calendar; truly the Bright Emperor simply clasped his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengguang's rule of years, the bright sovereign merely bowed in his seat.

sentences.zh: 曾問政於上學，著為君而我齒。

translations.literal: Once he questioned government in higher learning; in writing for the ruler I took my place.
translations.idiomatic: Once politics was asked at the higher academy; I set my teeth among those who wrote for the throne.

sentences.zh: 叫閽人以望予，遂陟降於庭止。

translations.literal: Calling the gateman to look for me, then ascending and descending on the court's step.
translations.idiomatic: The gate-keeper was called to seek me; then I climbed and came down the court stair.

sentences.zh: 同崔駰之謁帝，若謝兼之來仕。

translations.literal: Like Cui Yin's paying homage to the emperor, like Xie Kun's coming to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Like Cui Yin's audience with the ruler, like Xie Kun's coming to office.

sentences.zh: [3]逮孝莊之入統，乃道喪而時昏。

translations.literal: [3] Then when Xiaozhuang entered the succession, the Way was lost and the time dark.
translations.idiomatic: [3] When Xiaozhuang took the line, the Way failed and the age turned dim.

sentences.zh: 水羣飛於溟海，火載燎於中原。

translations.literal: Waters in flocks flew over the dark sea; fire laden burned across the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: Seas churned with swarming waves; flame rode the heartland's breadth.

sentences.zh: 延膠船而越水，若朽索而乘奔。

translations.literal: Prolonging the glued boat to cross the water, as if on rotten rope to ride the gallop.
translations.idiomatic: They bridged seas with boats of glue, or galloped on ropes already rotted.

sentences.zh: 玉羊失而無御，金雞亡而不存。

translations.literal: The jade ram lost with none to drive; the golden rooster gone and no more preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The jade sheep wandered driverless; the golden cock vanished, never to return.

sentences.zh: 天步忽其多難，橫流且其云始。

translations.literal: Heaven's steps suddenly many in difficulty; the crossflow and its cloud-beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's course turned sudden hardship; the flood-tide raised its first cloud.

sentences.zh: 既雲擾而海沸，亦岳立而棊峙。

translations.literal: Already clouds tumultuous and seas boiling, also peaks standing and wedges planted.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds boiled and seas heaved; mountains stood like chess pieces planted.

sentences.zh: 睇三綱之日紊，見四維之不理。

translations.literal: Gazing at the three bonds daily tangled, seeing the four corners not governed.
translations.idiomatic: I watched the three bonds fray day by day; the four pillars stood ungoverned.

sentences.zh: 顧茂草以傷懷，視匪車而思起。

translations.literal: Turning to view luxuriant grass in wounded heart, viewing the wrong cart and thinking to rise.
translations.idiomatic: I glanced at rich grass and felt the wound; I saw the misguided carriage and wished to act.

sentences.zh: 雖風雨之如晦，亮膠喈而不已。

translations.literal: Though wind and rain like darkness, yet bright glue and twitter unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Though wind and rain were twilight, still dawn-chirp and bright friendship did not cease.

sentences.zh: 自牽役於宰朝，實有懷於胥耻。

translations.literal: Since being dragged into service at the ministerial court, truly I had feeling of common shame.
translations.idiomatic: Dragged into the chief minister's service, I felt the court's shame in my own bones.

sentences.zh: 在下僚而栖屑，願奮迅於泥滓。

translations.literal: Beneath the inferior ranks I huddled in fragments; I wished to exert myself from muddy mire.
translations.idiomatic: A low clerk, I sat in broken pieces; yet I yearned to surge up from the slime.

sentences.zh: 眷故鄉以臨睨，悵有動於思歸。

translations.literal: Gazing at the native district in descent overlooking, grief had motion toward thinking of return.
translations.idiomatic: I looked toward home from afar; longing stirred to return.

sentences.zh: 越來流以鼓枻，遡北風而結騑。

translations.literal: Crossing the incoming current to beat the oar, tracing the north wind to tie the carriage teams.
translations.idiomatic: I rowed against the inflow; I harnessed teams into the north wind's way.

sentences.zh: 入成都之舊宅，反觀津之故扉。

translations.literal: Entering Chengdu's old residence, turning back to Guanjin's old doors.
translations.idiomatic: I entered Chengdu's former seat; I turned back to Guanjin's old gate.

sentences.zh: 乃曲肱而不悶，信抱甕而無機。

translations.literal: Then crooking the arm without affliction, truly embracing the jar without scheme.
translations.idiomatic: I bent my arm and was not vexed; I held the earthen jar and had no plot.

sentences.zh: 且耕而食，且蠶而衣。

translations.literal: Both plowing and eating, both raising silkworms and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Some fields I plowed to eat; some mulberry I tended for clothes.

sentences.zh: 恒一日以自省，亦三月而無違。

translations.literal: Constantly one day for self-examination, also three months without violation.
translations.idiomatic: Each day brought self-scrutiny; three months passed without breach.

sentences.zh: 遊仁義之肴覈，採墳素之精微。

translations.literal: Wandering the feast of benevolence and righteousness, gathering the subtle of the tomb-classics.
translations.idiomatic: I roamed the fare of humaneness and right; I culled the finesse of the classical tomes.

sentences.zh: 誠因閑而養拙，亦有樂於嘉肥。

translations.literal: Truly through leisure nourishing clumsiness, also having joy in fine fat.
translations.idiomatic: In idleness I nursed my awkwardness—and found joy even in good pasture.

sentences.zh: 及勾芒御節，姑洗之首，散遲遲於麗日，發依依於弱柳。

translations.literal: And when Gou Mang held the season, at the head of Gu washing—the sun lingered slow in beauty, and the weak willow sent forth reluctant tendrils.
translations.idiomatic: When Gou Mang ruled the season and Gu led the months, the fair sun loitered, and pale willows put out tender shoots.

sentences.zh: 鳥間關以呼庭，花芬披而落牖。

translations.literal: Birds interlocked in calling within the courtyard; flowers in fragrance spreading fell through the window.
translations.idiomatic: Birds called back and forth in the yard; scented blossoms drifted through the casement.

sentences.zh: 聽乃越於笙簧，望有踰於新婦。

translations.literal: Hearing surpassed the reed-pipe and gong; sight exceeded the new bride.
translations.idiomatic: What I heard outdid pipe and reed; what I saw outdid a bride's first glow.

sentences.zh: 襲成服以逍遙，願良辰而聊厚。

translations.literal: Assuming full dress for ease at large, wishing for good hours to make the day rich.
translations.idiomatic: In formal robes I wandered freely, hoping for a fine hour to thicken delight.

sentences.zh: 乃席壠而踞石，遂嘯儔而命偶。

translations.literal: Then spreading mat on the tumulus and perching on stone, thereupon whistling to companions and bidding them join.
translations.idiomatic: We spread mats on the low knoll and sat on stone, whistled to friends, and chose our mates.

sentences.zh: 同浴沂之五六，似禊洛之八九。

translations.literal: Together bathing in Yi like five or six, resembling the Luo purification's eight or nine.
translations.idiomatic: Like five or six bathing in the Yi, like eight or nine at the Luo rite of spring.

sentences.zh: 或促膝以持肩，或援笙而鼓缶。

translations.literal: Some pressing knees and holding shoulders, some drawing the reed-pipe and beating the jar.
translations.idiomatic: Some sat knee to knee, shoulder to shoulder; some took up pipes and drummed on clay pots.

sentences.zh: 賓奉萬年之觴，主報千金之壽。

translations.literal: The guest offered the cup of ten thousand years; the host returned the longevity of a thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: Guests raised the cup of ten thousand years; the host answered with wishes for a thousand-weight of life.

sentences.zh: 各笑語而卒獲，傳禮儀於不朽。

translations.literal: Each with laughter and speech at last attained, transmitting ritual and etiquette to no perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Each found laughter and talk at last, and passed rites and courtesy into what does not die.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋先民之所樂，而余心之所守也。

translations.literal: This covers what the ancient people rejoiced in, and what my heart keeps.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the joy of the ancients—and such is what my heart holds to.

sentences.zh: 至於少昊為帝，庚辛處躔，視墟里之蕭蕭，過寒夜之綿綿。

translations.literal: As for Shaohao as emperor, Geng and Xin in their stations—viewing hamlets desolate and sparse, passing cold nights long and fine.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaohao ruled and Geng and Xin held their stations, I saw hamlets thinned to silence and passed nights of endless cold.

sentences.zh: 積霜靄於近援，起泬寥於遠天。

translations.literal: Frost mist piled on near supports; vast emptiness rose in the far sky.
translations.idiomatic: Frost-haze banked close at hand; far heaven lifted into boundless hush.

sentences.zh: 思多端以類長，若臨水而登山。

translations.literal: Thoughts many-ended lengthened by kind, as if facing water while climbing a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughts branched and lengthened like climbing a mountain while staring at water below.

sentences.zh: 幸出遊之或寫，冀觀濤之可蠲。

translations.literal: Fortunate if outing might pour forth feeling; hoping to view the surge and be cleansed.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped an outing might ease the heart, that watching the tide could wash grief away.

sentences.zh: 遂杖策緩步，或漁或田。

translations.literal: Then with staff and bridle I walked slowly, sometimes fishing, sometimes farming.
translations.idiomatic: So I took staff and walked at ease, fishing one day, tilling the next.

sentences.zh: 弋鳧雁於清溪，釣魴鯉於深泉。

translations.literal: I shot ducks and geese on the clear stream; angled for bream and carp in the deep spring.
translations.idiomatic: I shot wildfowl on clear streams and angled for bream and carp in deep springs.

sentences.zh: 張廣幕，布長筵。

translations.literal: Spreading a broad awning, laying a long banquet.
translations.idiomatic: We spread wide awnings and set a long feast.

sentences.zh: 酌濁酒，割芳鮮。

translations.literal: Pouring thick wine, cutting fragrant fresh fare.
translations.idiomatic: We poured rough wine and sliced fresh delicacies.

sentences.zh: 起白雪於促柱，奉綠水於危弦。

translations.literal: Raising White Snow on the close pegs, offering Green Waters on the high strings.
translations.idiomatic: White Snow rose from tight pegs; Green Waters ran along taut strings.

sentences.zh: 賦湛露而不已，歌驪駒而未旋。

translations.literal: Chanting Dew without cease, singing the Parting Steed without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: We recited Dew without end and sang the Parting Steed, not yet turning homeward.

sentences.zh: 跌蕩世俗之外，疏散造化之間。

translations.literal: Tumbling outside the vulgar world, scattered between creation and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: We wandered beyond the world's dust, loose between heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 人生行樂，聊用永年。

translations.literal: Human life acts joy—for a while to extend the years.
translations.idiomatic: To live is to take joy—enough, for now, to lengthen one's years.

sentences.zh: 悟柱下之稱工，聞首陽之為拙。

translations.literal: I understood the pillar-below called skilled; I heard Shouyang called clumsy.
translations.idiomatic: I saw why the archivist was praised as skilled, and why Shouyang was called dull.

sentences.zh: 既有惜於苽懸，且自悲於井渫。

translations.literal: Already pity for the gourd hung up; also self-grief at the well rope drawn.
translations.idiomatic: I pitied the gourd left hanging unused and grieved for myself, rope at the well never lowered.

sentences.zh: 訪鄭詹之格言，求季主之高說。

translations.literal: I visited Zheng Zhan's fine words and sought the Ji Master's lofty discourse.
translations.idiomatic: I sought Zheng Zhan's pointed sayings and the Ji Master's high teachings.

sentences.zh: 去衡門以策駟，望象魏而投轍。

translations.literal: Leaving the humble gate with four horses whipped, gazing at the elephant gate-tower and turning the carriage track.
translations.idiomatic: I left my humble gate with four horses at the rein and, sighting the gate-towers, turned my carriage toward court.

sentences.zh: 服毳衣以從務，乘大車而就列。

translations.literal: Putting on fur coat to follow duties, riding the great cart to take my place in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I donned fur robes for service and rode the great carriage into rank.

sentences.zh: 比汗海而無紀，喻江河而有缺。

translations.literal: Compared to a sea of sweat without measure; likened to rivers with gaps.
translations.idiomatic: My toil was like a shoreless sea of sweat; my days like rivers that never ran full.

sentences.zh: 眷重地而懼深，念索米而慚結。

translations.literal: Attached to heavy office yet fearing the depth; thinking of seeking rice, shame knotted.
translations.idiomatic: I clung to weighty post yet feared its depth, and thought of begging rice—shame tied in knots.

sentences.zh: 運有折於玉斗，時忽亡於金鏡。

translations.literal: Fortune had a break in the jade dipper; the time suddenly lost the golden mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Fate snapped the jade ladle; the age suddenly lost its golden mirror.

sentences.zh: 始蒙塵以播蕩，卒流彘而居鄭。

translations.literal: At first dust covered us in turmoil; at last fleeing to Liuzhu, dwelling in Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At first the throne was dust and turmoil; at last the ruler fled to Liuzhu and lodged in Zheng.

sentences.zh: 彼上天之降鑒，實下民之請命。

translations.literal: That Heaven above sent down its mirror—truly the lower people pleaded for life.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven above cast down its gaze; the people below cried out for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 因艱難以隆基，據殷憂而啟聖。

translations.literal: Through hardship he raised the pinnacle; resting on deep sorrow he opened the sage.
translations.idiomatic: From hardship he raised the height of rule; from deep grief he opened the way of the sage.

sentences.zh: 調南風以負扆，居北辰而為政。

translations.literal: He tuned the south wind to lean on the arm-rest; dwelt at the north star and governed.
translations.idiomatic: He set the south wind to his back-rest and ruled from the pole star's seat.

sentences.zh: 創彝倫於九疇，班平章於百姓。

translations.literal: He created constant norms in the nine fields; distributed even clarity among the hundred clans.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the great norms in the nine domains and spread fair governance among the people.

sentences.zh: 喻繩契以論蹤，援成昭而比盛。

translations.literal: He likened cord and notch to trace the path; drew on Cheng and Zhao to match splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He matched cord and tally to chart the past and matched Cheng and Zhao in glory.

sentences.zh: 酌徙鎬之故典，究遷亳之遺令。

translations.literal: He drew from the old statutes of moving to Hao; examined the leftover orders of shifting to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He weighed the old statutes of the move to Hao and studied the lingering orders of the shift to Bo.

sentences.zh: 奄四海以為家，開七百而增慶。

translations.literal: He embraced the four seas as his house; opened seven hundred years and added celebration.
translations.idiomatic: He took the four seas as his house and opened seven hundred years of growing blessing.

sentences.zh: 覩禮樂之方隆，信光華之始映。

translations.literal: I saw ritual and music just rising; trusted that splendor had begun to shine.
translations.idiomatic: I saw rites and music on the rise and believed glory had begun to gleam.

sentences.zh: 百揆鬱以時序，四門穆其惟清。

translations.literal: The hundred duties flourished in season; the four gates were solemn, purely clear.
translations.idiomatic: All offices thrived in their seasons; the four gates stood serene and clear.

sentences.zh: 如得人於漢世，比多士於周庭。

translations.literal: Like gaining men in the Han age; compared to many scholars in the Zhou court.
translations.idiomatic: It was like finding men in Han times, like the many scholars in the Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 有一匡以作相，或十亂而為楨。

translations.literal: Some with one straightening became chief minister; some of the ten disordered became corner posts.
translations.idiomatic: Some with one correction became chief minister; some among the ten disordered served as corner pillars.

sentences.zh: 各秉文而經武，故天平而地成。

translations.literal: Each held culture and threaded military affairs; therefore heaven balanced and earth formed.
translations.idiomatic: Each held the brush and threaded the spear, until heaven balanced and earth held firm.

sentences.zh: 伊余身之忝穢，得再入於承明。

translations.literal: Alas—my person stained and base, yet I gained twice to enter Chenming.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I, stained and unworthy, was admitted twice to Chenming Hall.

sentences.zh: 執綸言之猶紼，戴會弁之如星。

translations.literal: Holding imperial words like mourning ties; wearing the meeting cap like stars.
translations.idiomatic: I held imperial words like funeral cords and wore the court cap bright as stars.

sentences.zh: 非巡潰以窺井，信夕惕而懷驚。

translations.literal: Not patrolling the breach to peer into the well; truly evening caution with fear in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: I did not skirt the dike to peer into the well, yet each night I stayed wary and afraid.

sentences.zh: 承周任之有言，攬老子之知足。

translations.literal: I received Zhou Ren's saying and embraced Laozi's knowing sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: I took Zhou Ren's words to heart and embraced Laozi's teaching of enough.

sentences.zh: 奉烱誡以周旋，抱徽猷而與屬。

translations.literal: I upheld bright admonitions in turning about and clasped fine designs as my charge.
translations.idiomatic: I kept bright warnings close in daily turn and held fine counsel as my trust.

sentences.zh: 每有偃於唯塵，恒興言於寵辱。

translations.literal: Often I rested in mere dust; constantly I spoke of favor and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Often I lay down in nothing but dust and spoke again and again of favor and fall.

sentences.zh: 思散髮以抽簪，願全真而守朴。

translations.literal: I thought to loosen hair and draw out the hairpin; wished to keep wholeness and guard simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: I thought to let my hair fall loose and pull out the pin, to keep my wholeness and hold to plainness.

sentences.zh: 眷疏傅以徘徊，望申公而躑躅。

translations.literal: I yearned toward Shu Fu and lingered; gazed at Lord Shen and hesitated on the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: I lingered toward Shu Fu's path and halted, gazing toward Lord Shen, unable to step forward.

sentences.zh: 冀鄙志之獲展，庶微願之逢時。

translations.literal: I hoped my humble aim might unfold; perhaps my slight wish would meet its season.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped my low wish might open, that my small desire might meet its hour.

sentences.zh: 歌致命而可卜，詠歸田而有期。

translations.literal: I sang that giving life could be divined; I chanted return to fields with a set term.
translations.idiomatic: I sang that surrendering life could be foretold and chanted return to the fields with a date in sight.

sentences.zh: 揖帝城以高逝，與人事而長辭。

translations.literal: I bowed to the imperial city and departed on high; with human affairs I took long farewell.
translations.idiomatic: I bowed to the imperial city and went away aloft, taking long leave of worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 擊壤而頌，結草而嬉。

translations.literal: Beating clods in praise, tying grass for play.
translations.idiomatic: I beat the clod in praise and wove grass for sport.

sentences.zh: 援巢父以戲潁，追許子而升箕。

translations.literal: I drew on Nest-Father to sport on the Ying; followed Master Xu to climb Ji.
translations.idiomatic: I called on Nest Father to play by the Ying and followed Master Xu up Mount Ji.

sentences.zh: 供暮餐於沆瀣，給朝餌於瓊芝。

translations.literal: Evening meals from the night dew; morning fare from jade fungus.
translations.idiomatic: Evening meals came from the night dew; morning food from jade fungus.

sentences.zh: 同糟醨而無別，混名實而不治。

translations.literal: Same lees and vinegar without distinction; mingling name and reality without governing.
translations.idiomatic: I shared lees and vinegar without distinction and mixed name and fact without ruling either.

sentences.zh: 放言肆慾，無慮無思。

translations.literal: Loosing words and indulging desire, without worry, without thought.
translations.idiomatic: I let words run free and desire roam, without care, without scheme.

sentences.zh: 何鷦鷯之可賦，鴻鵠之為詩哉。

translations.literal: Why compose on the wren? Why make verse of the swan?
translations.idiomatic: Why write rhapsodies on the wren, or poems on the great swan?

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍、殷州大中正、鎮南將軍、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Cadet Regular Palace Attendant, Grand Rectifier of Yin Province, General Who Guards the South, and Left Assistant in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further appointed cadet regular palace attendant, grand rectifier of Yin Province, general who guards the south, and left assistant minister of works.

sentences.zh: 仍以本官兼散騎常侍使蕭衍。

translations.literal: Still with his original office he concurrently served as Cadet Regular Palace Attendant on mission to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his original posts while also serving as cadet regular palace attendant on embassy to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免，論者以為非罪。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for an offense; commentators held it was not a true crime.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for an offense, though commentators held he was not guilty.

sentences.zh: 騫嘗贈親友盧元明、魏收詩曰：「幽棲多暇日，總駕萃荒坰。

translations.literal: Qian once presented a poem to his close friends Lu Yuanming and Wei Shou, saying: "In secluded dwelling many idle days; all carriages gather on the wild border."
translations.idiomatic: Qian once gave his friends Lu Yuanming and Wei Shou a poem that begins: "Secluded life leaves many idle days; our whole train meets on the wild outskirts."

sentences.zh: 南瞻帶宮雉，北睇拒畦瀛。

translations.literal: Southward I gaze on the belted palace pheasants; northward I look on fields that refuse the sea-mist.
translations.idiomatic: South I look on palace pheasants along the belt-wall; north I gaze on fields that hold back the misty flats.

sentences.zh: 流火時將末，懸炭漸云輕。

translations.literal: The Fire Star's season nears its end; the hanging charcoal grows light, they say.
translations.idiomatic: The Fire Star's season draws to its close; the hanging charcoal, they say, turns light.

sentences.zh: 寒風率已厲，秋水寂無聲。

translations.literal: The cold wind has already turned sharp; autumn waters are silent without sound.
translations.idiomatic: The cold wind has already turned harsh; autumn waters lie silent, without a sound.

sentences.zh: 層陰蔽長野，凍雨暗窮汀。

translations.literal: Layered shade covers the long wilds; freezing rain darkens the far shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Layered shade blankets the long wilds; freezing rain dims the distant shallows.

sentences.zh: 侶浴浮還沒，孤飛息且驚。

translations.literal: Companions bathing float and sink again; a lone flight rests yet starts in fright.
translations.idiomatic: Mates that bathed float up and sink again; a lone bird settles, then starts in fright.

sentences.zh: 三褫俄終歲，一丸曾未營。

translations.literal: Three dismissals soon ended the year; one pellet was never prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Three dismissals soon closed the year; one pellet of medicine was never prepared.

sentences.zh: 閑居同洛涘，歸身款武城。

translations.literal: Idle dwelling like the Luo shore; returning the body in courtesy to Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Idle living like the Luo bank; I return my person in trust to Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 稍旅原思藋，坐夢尹懃荊。

translations.literal: Briefly lodging with Yuan Si's mugwort; sitting, I dream Yin Qin's thorns.
translations.idiomatic: For a while I lodge with Yuan Si's mugwort bed; seated, I dream Yin Qin's thorny path.

sentences.zh: 監河愛斗水，蘇子惜餘明。

translations.literal: The river overseer loves a dipper of water; Master Su pities the remaining light.
translations.idiomatic: The river overseer cherishes a dipper of water; Master Su grieves the last of the light.

sentences.zh: 益州達友趣，[4]廷尉辯交情。

translations.literal: The Regional Inspector of Yizhou understood friendship's pull; [4] the Minister of Justice disputed the claim of affection.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Yizhou grasped friendship's pull; [4] the minister of justice argued over bonds of affection.

sentences.zh: 豈若忻蓬蓽，收志偶沉冥。

translations.literal: How like rejoicing in bramble-thatched huts, gathering the will to sink with the dark unseen.
translations.idiomatic: Better to delight in thatched huts and gather one's will to sink into the hidden dark.

sentences.zh: 」後詔兼太府少卿。

translations.literal: " Later an edict made him concurrently Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter an edict appointed him concurrently vice director of the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 尋除征南將軍、給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to General Who Campaigns South and Secretariat Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed general who campaigns south and secretariat gentleman of the yellow gate in attendance.

sentences.zh: 死於晉陽。

translations.literal: He died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦碑誄，別有集錄。

translations.literal: His compositions in poetry, fu, stele inscriptions, and dirges are separately collected in a recorded anthology.
translations.idiomatic: His poems, rhapsodies, stele texts, and dirges are recorded in a separate collected volume.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、太常、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former generalship, Minister of Ceremonies, and Governor of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former generalship, the ministry of ceremonies, and the governorship of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，重贈使持節、侍中、都督殷滄二州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，仍殷州刺史，諡曰文惠。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was again posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Yin and Cang Provinces, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Threefold Peer with the Three Excellencies, still Governor of Yin Province, posthumous name Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, he was again posthumously granted bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs for Yin and Cang provinces, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and threefold peer with the three excellencies, still as governor of Yin Province, with the posthumous name Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 騫弟希禮，字景節。

translations.literal: Qian's younger brother was Xili, styled Jingjie.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's younger brother Xili was styled Jingjie.

sentences.zh: 武定末，通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era he was Regular Attendant Direct and Upright in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuding he was regular attendant direct and upright in the palace.

sentences.zh: 希遠庶長兄長劍，[5]興和中，梁州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: Xiyuan's eldest son by a concubine was Changjian; [5] in the Xinghe era he was Chief Clerk of the Liang Province Rapid Cavalry Commandery Office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan's eldest son by a concubine was Changjian; [5] during the Xinghe period he served as chief clerk of the Liang Province Rapid Cavalry headquarters.

sentences.zh: 式弟弈，字景世。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother was Yi, styled Jingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Yi was styled Jingshi.

sentences.zh: 美容貌，有才藝。

translations.literal: He had a handsome appearance and possessed talent in the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in appearance, gifted in the arts.

sentences.zh: 早歷顯職，散騎常侍、宿衞監、都官尚書，安平侯。

translations.literal: Early he passed through eminent offices: Cadet Regular Palace Attendant, Night Guard Supervisor, Minister of the Capital Offices, and Marquis of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early to eminent posts: cadet regular palace attendant, night guard supervisor, minister of the capital offices, and Marquis of Anping.

sentences.zh: 與兄敷同死。

translations.literal: He died together with his elder brother Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He died together with his elder brother Fu.

sentences.zh: 太和初，文明太后追念弈兄弟，乃誅李訢，存問憲等一二家，[6]歲時賜以布帛。

translations.literal: Early in the Taihe era the Civilized Empress Dowager recalled Yi's brothers; she then executed Li Xin, inquired after Xian and one or two other households, [6] and at the seasons granted them cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe the Civilized Empress Dowager, remembering Yi's brothers, had Li Xin executed, sent inquiries to Xian and one or two other households, [6] and at the seasons granted them cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 弈別生弟冏，字道度。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother by a different mother was Jiong, styled Daodu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger half-brother Jiong was styled Daodu.

sentences.zh: 少為中散。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as a regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 逃避得免。

translations.literal: He fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He fled and escaped death.

sentences.zh: 太和中，拜下大夫、南部給事。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was appointed Lower Grand Master and Attendant of the Southern Section.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was appointed lower grand master and attendant of the southern section.

sentences.zh: 出為龍驤將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General of the Dragon Might and Governor of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as general of the dragon might and governor of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，拜冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed General Who Wins the Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed general who wins the campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋除光祿大夫，守度支尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed grand master of splendid happiness and acting minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，高祖幸長安，冏以咸陽山河險固，秦漢舊都，古稱陸海，勸高祖去洛陽而都之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the High Ancestor visited Chang'an; Jiong, because Xianyang's mountains and rivers were perilous and firm, the Qin and Han old capital, anciently called the land-sea, urged the High Ancestor to leave Luoyang and make it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the High Ancestor visited Chang'an; Jiong, noting that Xianyang's mountains and rivers were strong, that it was the old capital of Qin and Han and anciently called the land-sea, urged him to leave Luoyang and establish his capital there.

sentences.zh: 後高祖引見，笑而謂之曰：「卿一昨有啟，欲朕都此。

translations.literal: Later the High Ancestor summoned him for audience, smiled, and said to him: "You recently had a memorial wishing that We make this Our capital."
translations.idiomatic: Later the High Ancestor received him and said with a smile, "You recently memorialized wishing that We make this Our capital."

sentences.zh: 昔婁敬一說，漢祖即日西駕。

translations.literal: Formerly Lou Jing spoke once and the Han Founder that very day drove west.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lou Jing spoke, and the Han founder that very day turned his carriage west.

sentences.zh: 尚書今以西京說朕，仍使朕不廢東轅，當是獻可理殊，所以今古相反耳。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat urged Us with the western capital, yet still kept Us from abandoning the eastern axle—surely the offered plan and its reason differ, hence ancient and present oppose each other.
translations.idiomatic: Our director of the secretariat urged the western capital on Us, yet still kept Us from abandoning the eastern road—the case offered and its logic must differ, and so ancient and present run opposite.

sentences.zh: 」冏對曰：「昔漢祖起於布衣，欲藉嶮以自固，婁敬之言，合於本旨。

translations.literal: " Jiong replied: "Formerly the Han Founder rose from common cloth, wished to rely on peril to secure himself—the words of Lou Jing matched his basic aim."
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong replied, "Formerly the Han founder rose from common cloth and wished to rely on perilous ground to secure himself; Lou Jing's words matched that aim."

sentences.zh: 今陛下百世重光，德洽四海，事同隆周，均其職貢，是以愚臣獻說，不能上動。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's hundred generations shine anew, virtue reaches the four seas, affairs match the lofty Zhou, all alike in tribute and duty—therefore this foolish minister's offered counsel could not stir you on high.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's hundred generations shine anew, your virtue fills the four seas, your affairs match the lofty Zhou, and all realms bring equal tribute—so this foolish minister's counsel could not move you.

sentences.zh: 」高祖大悅。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Ancestor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 其年冏卒。

translations.literal: That year Jiong died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jiong died.

sentences.zh: 賜錢二十萬，布百匹，朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was granted two hundred thousand in cash, a hundred bolts of cloth, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted two hundred thousand cash, a hundred bolts of cloth, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.

sentences.zh: 冏性鯁烈，敢直言，常面折高祖，彈駁公卿，無所回避，百僚皆憚之。

translations.literal: Jiong's nature was blunt and fierce; he dared speak plainly, often rebuking the High Ancestor to his face and impeaching dukes and ministers without shrinking from anyone—all the hundred offices feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was blunt and fierce by nature; he dared speak plainly, often rebuking the High Ancestor to his face and impeaching dukes and ministers without shrinking from anyone, and every officeholder feared him.

sentences.zh: 高祖常加優禮，故車駕巡幸，恒兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor often added exceptional courtesy; hence when the imperial carriage went on inspection tours, he constantly also held Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor often treated him with special favor; hence whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, he was regularly also right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 雖才學不及諸兄，然公強當世，堪濟過之。

translations.literal: Though his talent and learning did not reach his elder brothers, yet his public forcefulness in his age exceeded what they could accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: Though his learning and talent did not match his elder brothers, his public forcefulness in his age surpassed what they could achieve.

sentences.zh: 子祐，字長禧。

translations.literal: His son You, styled Changxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son You was styled Changxi.

sentences.zh: 篤穆友于，見稱於世。

translations.literal: Deeply earnest and friendly toward his brothers, he was praised in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply earnest and brotherly, he won praise throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 歷位給事中、尚書祠部郎、相州撫軍府長史、司空從事中郎、博陵太守。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Supervising Secretary, Secretariat Master of Sacrifices, chief steward of the Pacifying-Army headquarters of Xiang Province, attendant gentleman of the Minister of Works, and Administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supervising secretary, secretariat master of sacrifices, chief steward of the pacifying-army headquarters in Xiang Province, attendant gentleman to the minister of works, and administrator of Boling.

sentences.zh: 所在亦以清幹著稱。

translations.literal: In every place he likewise was famed for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he was likewise noted for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 祐弟太，字季寧。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Tai, styled Jining.
translations.idiomatic: You's younger brother Tai was styled Jining.

sentences.zh: 涉歷書傳。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and historical records.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged widely through books and historical records.

sentences.zh: 太尉行軍員外郎。

translations.literal: Extraordinary officer on the staff of the Grand Marshal's campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He served as extraordinary officer on the grand marshal's campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 順弟修基，陳留太守。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Xiuji, Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Xiuji served as administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子探幽。

translations.literal: His son Tan You.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Tan You.

sentences.zh: 探幽兄子洪鸞，河間太守。

translations.literal: Tan You's elder brother's son Hongluan, Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Tan You's elder brother's son Hongluan served as administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 洪鸞孫悕傑，樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Hongluan's grandson Xijie, Administrator of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Hongluan's grandson Xijie served as administrator of Leling.

sentences.zh: 武定中，以貪汙賜死。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, for corruption he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he was sentenced to death for corruption.

sentences.zh: 脩基季弟惲，字善祖，小字藥囊。

translations.literal: Xiuji's youngest younger brother Yun, styled Shanzu, pet name Medicine Pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuji's youngest younger brother Yun was styled Shanzu; his pet name was Medicine Pouch.

sentences.zh: 少有高名，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In youth he had a lofty reputation and served as Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he enjoyed a lofty reputation and served as secretariat vice director.

sentences.zh: 從世祖征涼州，戰沒。

translations.literal: He followed the Shizu emperor on the expedition to Liang Province and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Shizu on the Liangzhou campaign and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 時人咸惜焉。

translations.literal: People of the time all mourned it.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time all lamented his loss.

sentences.zh: 初順與從兄靈、從弟孝伯並以學識器業見重於時，故能砥礪宗族，競各修尚。

translations.literal: At first Shun, together with his cousin Ling and his cousin Xiaobo, were all esteemed in their day for learning and capacity; thus they could sharpen the clan, each striving to cultivate himself.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shun, his cousin Ling, and his cousin Xiaobo were all esteemed for learning and capacity; they sharpened the clan, and each strove to cultivate himself.

sentences.zh: 靈與族叔詵、族弟熙等俱被徵。

translations.literal: Ling, together with his clan uncle Shen, his clan younger brother Xi, and others, were all summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ling, his clan uncle Shen, his clan younger brother Xi, and others were all summoned to office.

sentences.zh: 事在高允高士頌。

translations.literal: The matter is in Gao Yong's Eulogy of Eminent Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in Gao Yong's Eulogy of Eminent Scholars.

translations.literal: Source annotation [7].
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note [7].

sentences.zh: 詵，字令孫。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Lingsun.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was styled Lingsun.

sentences.zh: 京兆太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 詵後繼。

translations.literal: Shen's descendants continued the line.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's line continued through his descendants.

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: Lacuna in the text.

sentences.zh: 秀林，小名榼。

translations.literal: Xiulin, pet name Jar.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulin's pet name was Jar.

sentences.zh: 性強直。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was firm and upright by nature.

sentences.zh: 太和中，自中書博士為頓丘相，豪右畏之。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, from Doctor of the Secretariat he became magistrate of Dunqiu; the powerful local families feared him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he rose from secretariat doctor to magistrate of Dunqiu, and the local magnates feared him.

sentences.zh: 景明初，試守博陵郡，批強扶弱，政以威嚴為名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, acting as administrator of Boling commandery, he struck down the strong and supported the weak; his government was famed for stern majesty.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era he acted as administrator of Boling, striking down the strong and supporting the weak; his rule was famed for stern authority.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 後為太尉諮議參軍，假節，行荊州事。

translations.literal: Later he was Counselor and Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal, with provisional tally, acting in the affairs of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as counselor and staff officer to the grand marshal, with provisional tally, acting in Jing Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 拜司徒司馬，加冠軍將軍、定州大中正、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Master of Ceremonies to the Minister of Education, with the added ranks of General Who Champions, chief Rectifier of Ding Province, and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed master of ceremonies to the minister of education, with the added ranks of general who champions, chief rectifier of Ding Province, and grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 正光中卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhengguang era, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhengguang era at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Left General and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the titles left general and governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 子裔，字徽伯。

translations.literal: His son Yi, styled Huibo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was styled Huibo.

sentences.zh: 出後秀林兄鳳林。

translations.literal: He was given in adoption to Xiulin's elder brother Fenglin.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted as heir to Xiulin's elder brother Fenglin.

sentences.zh: 裔初除汝南王悅常侍，稍遷定州別駕。

translations.literal: Yi was first removed to Regular Attendant to the Prince of Runan, Yue, then gradually promoted to Vice Administrator of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was first appointed regular attendant to the Prince of Runan, Yue, then gradually promoted to vice administrator of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，為定州鎮軍長史，加輔國將軍，帶博陵太守。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he was chief steward of the Pacifying-Army headquarters of Ding Province, with the added rank of General Who Assists the State, concurrently Administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he served as chief steward of the pacifying-army headquarters in Ding Province, with the added rank of general who assists the state and concurrent administrator of Boling.

sentences.zh: 于時逆賊杜洛周侵亂州界，尋假平北將軍，防城都督。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel Du Luozhou raided and disturbed the provincial borders; soon Yi was provisionally made General Who Pacifies the North and Defense-of-the-City Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebel Du Luozhou was ravaging the provincial borders; Yi was soon made provisional general who pacifies the north and commander for the defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 賊既圍城，裔潛引洛周，州遂陷沒。

translations.literal: Once the bandits had besieged the city, Yi secretly brought Luozhou in, and the province then fell.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels besieged the city, Yi secretly admitted Luozhou, and the province fell.

sentences.zh: 洛周僭竊，特無綱紀，至於市令驛帥，咸以為王，呼曰市王、驛王。

translations.literal: Luozhou usurped rule and was wholly without discipline; even market overseers and post-station chiefs were all made kings, called Market King and Post King.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou usurped power and kept no discipline at all—even market overseers and post-station chiefs were made kings, called the Market King and the Post King.

sentences.zh: 乃封裔為定州王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was enfeoffed as King of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yi was enfeoffed as king of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 洛周尋為葛榮所滅，裔仍事榮。

translations.literal: Luozhou was soon destroyed by Ge Rong, and Yi still served Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou was soon destroyed by Ge Rong, and Yi continued to serve Rong.

sentences.zh: 永安初，尒朱榮既擒葛榮，遂縶裔及高敖曹、薛脩義、李無為等於晉陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, after Erzhu Rong had captured Ge Rong, he then bound Yi together with Gao Aocao, Xue Xiuyi, Li Wuwei, and others at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yong'an era, after Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong, he bound Yi together with Gao Aocao, Xue Xiuyi, Li Wuwei, and others at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 從榮至洛。

translations.literal: He followed Rong to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Rong to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 榮死乃免。

translations.literal: When Rong died he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died he was released.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，以裔為持節、散騎常侍、安北將軍、兼給事黃門侍郎、慰勞山東大使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, Yi was made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, concurrent Secretariat Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in Attendance, and Grand Envoy to Console the East of the Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Putai era Yi was appointed bearer of the staff, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the north, concurrent secretariat gentleman of the yellow gate in attendance, and grand envoy to console the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，除鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫、齊獻武王大丞相諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was removed to General Who Guards the East, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Counselor and Staff Officer to the Grand Chancellor of the Prince of Qi, Xian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he was appointed general who guards the east, grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon, and counselor and staff officer to the grand chancellor of the Prince of Qi, Xian.

sentences.zh: 天平初，以預定策之功，封固安縣開國伯，食邑四百戶，加征東將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, for his merit in planning the decisive move beforehand, he was enfeoffed as founding Baron of Gu'an county with a fief of four hundred households, and additionally made General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianping era, for his merit in the prior planning of the coup, he was enfeoffed as founding baron of Gu'an with a fief of four hundred households and additionally made general who campaigns east.

sentences.zh: 車駕遷鄴，為大行臺右丞，留在洛陽，監修宮殿。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage moved to Ye, he was made Right Vice Director of the Grand Mobile Office, remained in Luoyang, and supervised the repair of the palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Ye, he became right vice director of the grand mobile office, remained in Luoyang, and supervised repairs to the palaces.

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、大將軍、陝州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Grand General, and Governor of Shan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed bearer of the staff with full credentials, grand general, and governor of Shan Province.

sentences.zh: [8]四年八月，宇文黑獺攻陷州城，被執見害，年五十。

translations.literal: [8] In the eighth month of the fourth year, Yuwen Heita attacked and took the provincial city; Yi was seized and killed, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: [8] In the eighth month of the fourth year Yuwen Heita captured the provincial city; Yi was seized and killed at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 詔贈使持節、都督定冀瀛殷四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、定州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ding, Ji, Ying, and Yin provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, Duke of the Minister of Education, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him bearer of the staff with full credentials, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ding, Ji, Ying, and Yin provinces, general of agile cavalry, director of the secretariat, duke of the minister of education, and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子直，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: [9]武定末，司徒屬。

translations.literal: [9] At the end of Wuding he was an aide in the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: [9] At the end of the Wuding era he served as an aide in the ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced as usual.

sentences.zh: 裔弟景義，大司馬諮議參軍、殷州大中正。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Jingyi, Counselor and Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal and chief Rectifier of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Jingyi served as counselor and staff officer to the grand marshal and chief rectifier of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 景義弟伯穆，武定末，合州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingyi's younger brother Bomu, at the end of Wuding Governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi's younger brother Bomu served at the end of the Wuding era as governor of He Province.

sentences.zh: 秀林從弟煥，字仲文，小字醜瓌。

translations.literal: Xiulin's cousin Huan, styled Zhongwen, pet name Ugly Jade.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulin's cousin Huan was styled Zhongwen; his pet name was Ugly Jade.

sentences.zh: 有幹用。

translations.literal: He had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed practical ability.

sentences.zh: 少與酈道元俱為李彪所知。

translations.literal: In youth he and Li Daoyuan were both recognized by Li Biao.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Li Daoyuan were both recognized by Li Biao.

sentences.zh: 自給事中轉治書侍御史。

translations.literal: From Supervising Secretary he was transferred to Attendant Imperial Censor with jurisdiction over documents.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from supervising secretary to attendant imperial censor with jurisdiction over documents.

sentences.zh: 恒州刺史穆泰據代都謀反，高祖詔煥與任城王澄推治之。

translations.literal: Governor of Heng Province Mu Tai seized the Dai capital and plotted rebellion; the High Ancestor ordered Huan and the Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Tai, governor of Heng Province, seized the Dai capital and plotted rebellion, the High Ancestor ordered Huan and the Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, to investigate and try the case.

sentences.zh: 煥先驅至州，宣旨曉喻，仍誅泰等。

translations.literal: Huan went ahead as vanguard to the province, proclaimed the imperial edict and enlightened the people, then executed Tai and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Huan went ahead to the province, proclaimed the imperial edict to explain the situation, and then executed Tai and his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 景明初，遷司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era he was transferred to attendant gentleman of the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶卷豫州刺史裴叔業以壽春歸附，詔煥以本官為軍司，與楊大眼、奚康生等率眾迎接。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baojuan's Governor of Yu Province Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun, an edict made Huan army steward in his present office, and with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others he led troops to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye, governor of Yu Province under Xiao Baojuan, surrendered Shouchun, an edict appointed Huan army steward in his present office; with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others he led troops to receive the city.

sentences.zh: 煥至淮西，叔業兄子植遣使送質。

translations.literal: When Huan reached the west of the Huai, Shuye's elder brother's son Zhi sent envoys to deliver hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan reached the Huai west, Shuye's elder brother's son Zhi sent envoys with hostages.

sentences.zh: 煥等濟師，入城撫慰，民咸忻悅。

translations.literal: Huan and the others crossed with the army, entered the city to console the people, and all the populace rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and his men crossed with the army, entered the city to reassure the people, and the populace rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 仍行揚州事，賜爵容城伯。

translations.literal: He then acted in the affairs of Yang Province and was granted the title Baron of Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then acted in Yang Province affairs and was granted the title baron of Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 軍還，行河內郡事。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he acted in the affairs of Henei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he acted in Henei commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 拜司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Chief Steward to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right chief steward to the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 以荊蠻擾動，敕煥兼散騎常侍慰勞之，降者萬餘家。

translations.literal: Because the Jing barbarians were in disturbance, an edict made Huan concurrently Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry to console them; more than ten thousand households submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing barbarians were in unrest, an edict appointed Huan concurrently regular attendant of the scattered cavalry to console them, and more than ten thousand households submitted.

sentences.zh: 除輔國將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was removed to General Who Assists the State and Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who assists the state and governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 時武興氐楊集起舉兵作逆，令弟集義邀斷白馬戍。

translations.literal: At that time the Di of Wuxing, Yang Jiq, raised troops in rebellion and ordered his younger brother Jiyi to intercept and cut off the White Horse garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Jiq of the Wuxing Di raised troops in rebellion and ordered his younger brother Jiyi to cut off the White Horse garrison.

sentences.zh: 敕假煥平西將軍，督別將石長樂、統軍王祐等與軍司苟金養俱討之，大破集起軍。

translations.literal: An edict provisionally made Huan General Who Pacifies the West, supervising detached generals Shi Changle, commandery commander Wang You, and others, together with army steward Gou Jinyang, to campaign against them; they smashed Jiq's army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict provisionally made Huan general who pacifies the west and put him in command of detached generals Shi Changle, commandery commander Wang You, and others, together with army steward Gou Jinyang, to campaign against them; they routed Jiq's army.

sentences.zh: 會秦州民呂苟兒反，煥仍令長樂等由麥積崖赴援。

translations.literal: It happened that the people of Qin Province, Lü Gou'er, rebelled; Huan still ordered Changle and the others to go by way of Maiji Cliff to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qinzhou native Lü Gou'er rebelled, Huan still ordered Changle and the others to march by Maiji Cliff to relieve the situation.

sentences.zh: 屬都督元麗至，遂共平之。

translations.literal: When the area commander Yuan Li arrived, they then together pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: When area commander Yuan Li arrived, they pacified the rebellion together.

sentences.zh: 時氐王楊定進猶據方山，與苟兒影響，煥密募氐趙芒路斬定進。

translations.literal: At that time the Di king Yang Dingjin still held Mount Fang and echoed Gou'er; Huan secretly recruited the Di Zhao Manglu to behead Dingjin on the road.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Di king Yang Dingjin still held Mount Fang in concert with Gou'er; Huan secretly recruited the Di Zhao Manglu to ambush and behead Dingjin.

sentences.zh: 還朝，遇患卒，時年四十四。

translations.literal: On returning to court he fell ill and died, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he fell ill and died at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰昭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Governor of You Province, with posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted general who campaigns against the barbarians and governor of You Province, with the posthumous title Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子密，武定中，襄州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Mi, in the Wuding era Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi served during the Wuding era as governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 秀林族子肅，字彥邕。

translations.literal: Xiulin's clansman Su, styled Yanyong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulin's clansman Su was styled Yanyong.

sentences.zh: 歷奉朝請，清河王懌郎中令。

translations.literal: He passed through Court Attendant in Regular Attendance and Master of the Household to the Prince of Qinghe, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as court attendant in regular attendance and master of the household to the Prince of Qinghe, Yi.

sentences.zh: 稍遷洛陽令、步兵校尉、員外常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Magistrate of Luoyang, Colonel of the Footsoldiers, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to magistrate of Luoyang, colonel of the footsoldiers, and extraordinary regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 初謟附侍中元暉，後以左道事侍中穆紹。

translations.literal: At first he fawned on Attendant-in-Chief Yuan Hui; later he served Attendant-in-Chief Mu Shao with heterodox practices.
translations.idiomatic: At first he fawned on attendant-in-chief Yuan Hui; later he served attendant-in-chief Mu Shao with heterodox rites.

sentences.zh: 常裸身被髮，畫腹銜刀，於隱屏之處為紹求福，故紹愛之。

translations.literal: He often went naked with hair unbound, painted his belly and held a knife in his mouth, and in hidden screened places sought blessings for Shao—therefore Shao favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He often went naked with hair unbound, painted his belly and held a knife between his teeth, and in hidden screened chambers performed rites to seek blessings for Shao—therefore Shao favored him.

sentences.zh: 延昌四年，薦肅為黃門郎，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanchang, he recommended Su as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, with the added rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yanchang era he recommended Su as gentleman of the yellow gate, with the added rank of grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 肅為性酒狂，熙平初從靈太后幸江陽王繼第，肅時侍飲，頗醉，言辭不遜，抗辱太傅、清河王懌，為有司彈劾。

translations.literal: Su by nature was given to wine and frenzy; at the beginning of Xiping, following Empress Dowager Ling on a visit to the mansion of the Prince of Jiangyang, Ji, Su was then attending the drinking, quite drunk, his words disrespectful, resisting and insulting the Grand Tutor, Prince of Qinghe, Yi—he was impeached by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Su was by nature given to wine and wild behavior; at the start of the Xiping era he accompanied Empress Dowager Ling on a visit to the Prince of Jiangyang's mansion, where he was attending the drinking, became quite drunk, spoke disrespectfully, and openly insulted the grand tutor, the Prince of Qinghe, Yi; the authorities impeached him.

sentences.zh: 靈太后怒之，出為章武內史。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was angry with him and sent him out as Internal Administrator of Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was angry with him and sent him out as internal administrator of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷右將軍、夏州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Right General and Governor of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to right general and governor of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was granted Left General and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the titles left general and governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 肅從弟曒，字景林。

translations.literal: Su's cousin Liao, styled Jinglin.
translations.idiomatic: Su's cousin Liao was styled Jinglin.

sentences.zh: 有學識。

translations.literal: He had learning and knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed learning and knowledge.

sentences.zh: 初除奉朝請，太學博士、司空主簿。

translations.literal: He was first removed to Court Attendant in Regular Attendance, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, and Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed court attendant in regular attendance, doctor of the imperial academy, and chief clerk to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜左軍將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was appointed general of the left army.

sentences.zh: 正光中，元叉以其弟羅為青州刺史，曒為羅平東府長史。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era, Yuan Cha made his younger brother Luo Governor of Qing Province, and Liao was Luo's chief steward of the Eastern Headquarters of Ping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era Yuan Cha appointed his younger brother Luo governor of Qing Province, and Liao served as Luo's chief steward of the eastern headquarters at Ping.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉少卿、殷州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Justice and Senior Rectifier of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the court of justice and senior rectifier of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年冬，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xiaochang he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the second year of Xiaochang, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、齊州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received the titles General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Qi Province; his posthumous name was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the titles general who pacifies the east and governor of Qi Province, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子慎，武定中，東平太守。

translations.literal: His son Shen; during Wuding he was Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen served as administrator of Dongping during Wuding.

sentences.zh: 曒從弟仲琁，奉朝請、定雍二州長史、太尉諮議、中散、太中大夫、東郡汲郡二郡太守、司徒左長史、弘農太守。

translations.literal: Qiao's younger cousin Zhongzhen served as Regular Attendant at Court, Chief Clerk of Ding and Yong provinces, Staff Counselor to the Grand Commander, Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Palace, Administrator of both Dong Commandery and Ji Commandery, Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat, and Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's younger cousin Zhongzhen held successive posts as regular attendant at court, chief clerk of Ding and Yong provinces, staff counselor to the grand commander, palace attendant, grand master of the palace, administrator of Dong and Ji commanderies, left chief clerk of the secretariat, and administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 先是，宮牛二姓阻嶮為害，仲琁示以威惠，並即歸伏。

translations.literal: Previously the Gong and Niu clans, taking advantage of rugged terrain, had caused harm; Zhongzhen displayed both might and kindness, and they at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Gong and Niu clans had preyed on the region from its rugged terrain; Zhongzhen showed them both force and favor, and they submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 還除衞將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed General of the Guard and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed general of the guard and grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 仍除北雍州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Governor of Northern Yong Province, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was then named governor of Northern Yong Province while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 轉車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of the chariots and cavalry and left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 天平初，遷都於鄴，以仲琁為營構將作，[10]進號衞大將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianping, when the capital was moved to Ye, Zhongzhen was made Director of Palace Construction for camp building,[10] and advanced in title to Grand General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianping, when the court moved the capital to Ye, Zhongzhen was appointed director of palace construction for the new works[10] and promoted to grand general of the guard.

sentences.zh: 出除車騎大將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as grand general of the chariots and cavalry and governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 仲琁以孔子廟牆宇頗有頹毀，遂修改焉。

translations.literal: Zhongzhen, seeing that the walls and buildings of Confucius's temple were rather dilapidated, then repaired them.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the walls and buildings of Confucius's temple in considerable decay, Zhongzhen had them repaired.

sentences.zh: 還，除將作大匠。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed master of works.

sentences.zh: 所歷並清勤有聲。

translations.literal: In every post he was alike famed for purity and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Every office he held won him renown for integrity and diligence.

sentences.zh: 年六十六，卒。

translations.literal: At age sixty-six he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received the titles Pillar-General of the Cavalry, Companionship Equaling the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the titles pillar-general of the cavalry, companionship equaling the three excellencies, and governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 子希良，侍御史。

translations.literal: His son Xiliang, Attending Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiliang served as attending imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 詵從子善，犯孝靜諱。

translations.literal: Shen's grand-nephew Shan offended the taboo name of Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's grand-nephew Shan had violated the taboo name of Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was administrator of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子顯進，州主簿。

translations.literal: His son Xianjin, Provincial Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianjin served as provincial registrar.

sentences.zh: 顯進子映，字輝道。

translations.literal: Xianjin's son Ying, styled Huidao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianjin's son Ying was styled Huidao.

sentences.zh: 南安王國常侍、光州征虜府主簿、相州治中、寧朔將軍、步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant of the Kingdom of Nan'an, Registrar of the Pacification-of-Barbarians Staff of Guang Province, Secretariat Assistant of Xiang Province, General Who Pacifies the North, and Colonel of the Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as regular attendant of the kingdom of Nan'an, registrar on the pacification-of-barbarians staff of Guang Province, secretariat assistant of Xiang Province, general who pacifies the north, and colonel of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 孝昌三年冬卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: He died in the winter of the third year of Xiaochang, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the third year of Xiaochang, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 天平中，贈通直散騎常侍、輔國將軍、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: During Tianping he was posthumously given the titles Regular Attendant of the Direct Channel, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was posthumously given the titles regular attendant of the direct channel, general who assists the state, and governor of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 子普濟，武定中，北海太守。

translations.literal: His son Puji; during Wuding he was Administrator of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Puji served as administrator of Beihai during Wuding.

sentences.zh: 映弟育，字仲遠。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Yu, styled Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Yu was styled Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regular attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 稍遷揚烈將軍、奉車都尉、都督相州防城別將。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General Who Displays Fierceness, Commandant of the Imperial Carriages, and Separate Commander overseeing the defense of Xiang Province's cities.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to general who displays fierceness, commandant of the imperial carriages, and separate commander in charge of defending the cities of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 以拒葛榮之勳，賜爵趙郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit in resisting Ge Rong he was granted the title Marquis of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in resisting Ge Rong he was enfeoffed as marquis of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後除征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed general who pacifies the east and grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 天平四年夏卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: He died in the summer of the fourth year of Tianping, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the fourth year of Tianping, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、都官尚書、定州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received the titles Pillar-General of the Cavalry, Minister of Justice, and Governor of Ding Province; his posthumous name was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the titles pillar-general of the cavalry, minister of justice, and governor of Ding Province, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子惜，襲。

translations.literal: His son Xi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定末，齊文襄王大將軍府記室參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Staff Recorder of the Grand General's Headquarters of Qi Prince Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he served as staff recorder in Prince Wenxiang of Qi's grand general headquarters.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his noble title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his noble title was reduced in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 顯進弟恃顯，位至左中郎將。

translations.literal: Xianjin's younger brother Shixian rose to the post of Left Commandant of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xianjin's younger brother Shixian rose to the post of left commandant of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中壘將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received the titles General of the Central Ramparts and Governor of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the titles general of the central ramparts and governor of An Province.

sentences.zh: 恃顯養京兆王愉妾楊氏為女，愉改楊姓為李，而親念恃顯。

translations.literal: Shixian raised the concubine Yang of the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, as his daughter; Yu changed the Yang surname to Li, yet was personally fond of Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian raised Prince Yu of Jingzhao's concubine Lady Yang as his own daughter; Yu changed her surname from Yang to Li, yet remained personally attached to Shixian.

sentences.zh: 恃顯子道舒與愉同逆。

translations.literal: Shixian's son Daoshu joined Yu in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian's son Daoshu joined Yu in his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 愉敗，走免。

translations.literal: When Yu was defeated, he fled and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was defeated, Daoshu fled and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 第三子道璩，武定末，范陽太守。

translations.literal: His third son Daoquan; at the end of Wuding he was Administrator of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Daoquan served as administrator of Fanyang at the end of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 道璩弟道瓘，少以父譴被刑，位至中常侍。

translations.literal: Daoquan's younger brother Daoguan, in his youth because of his father's reproach was punished by mutilation, and rose to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Daoquan's younger brother Daoguan had been punished with mutilation in his youth because of his father's offense, yet eventually rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 恃顯弟曄，字季顯，涉歷書史。

translations.literal: Shixian's younger brother Ye, styled Jixian, had ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian's younger brother Ye, styled Jixian, had studied the classics and histories thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: Acting Staff Officer of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting staff officer under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 稍遷濟州輔國府長史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Pacification-of-the-State Staff of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to chief clerk of the pacification-of-the-state staff of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 坐兄事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed because of his elder brother's case.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office on account of his elder brother's case.

sentences.zh: 後除尚書中兵郎，遷冠軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat's Military Bureau and transferred to Champion and Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed gentleman of the secretariat's military bureau, then promoted to champion and palace attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，南荊州刺史桓叔興驅掠城民，叛入蕭衍，衍資以兵糧，令築谷陂城以立洛州，逼土山戍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguang, Huan Shuxing of Southern Jing Province drove off and plundered the city populace, rebelled and entered Xiao Yan's service; Yan supplied him with troops and grain and ordered him to build Gubei city to establish Luo Province, pressing upon Tushan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguang, Huan Shuxing, governor of Southern Jing Province, drove off and plundered the city's people and defected to Xiao Yan, who supplied him with troops and grain and ordered him to build Gubei city to establish Luo Province and press upon Tushan garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔曄持節、兼尚書左丞為行臺，督諸軍討叔興，大破之。

translations.literal: The edict ordered Ye to bear the staff of authority and concurrently serve as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat as Mobile Commissioner, to supervise the various armies in punishing Shuxing, and he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Ye as commissioner bearing the staff of authority and concurrent left vice director of the secretariat, placed him in charge of the armies sent against Shuxing, and he won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 乘勝拔谷陂，叔興退走。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he took Gubei; Shuxing retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory, he captured Gubei, and Shuxing withdrew and fled.

sentences.zh: 軍還，仍除尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was appointed left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出除洛州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed Governor of Luo Province, his generalship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Luo Province while retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could take office he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received the titles General of the Left and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the titles general of the left and governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 子暉賓，美容貌，寬和沉雅。

translations.literal: His son Huibin was handsome in appearance, magnanimous, gentle, and refined in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huibin was handsome in appearance, open-hearted, gentle, and refined in manner.

sentences.zh: 太學博士。

translations.literal: Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He served as doctor of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 暉賓弟山儒，少而清立，學涉羣書。

translations.literal: Huibin's younger brother Shanru, from youth upright and pure, had studied many books.
translations.idiomatic: Huibin's younger brother Shanru had been upright and serious from youth and had read widely across the classics.

sentences.zh: 山儒少弟大蓋。

translations.literal: Shanru's youngest brother Dagai.
translations.idiomatic: Shanru's youngest brother was Dagai.

sentences.zh: 並早卒。

translations.literal: Both died young.
translations.idiomatic: Both died young.

sentences.zh: 曄族弟孝怡，字悅宗。

translations.literal: Ye's clan cousin Xiaoyi, styled Yuezong.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's clan cousin Xiaoyi was styled Yuezong.

sentences.zh: 中書學生、相州高陽王雍主簿、廣陵王羽掾、新蔡太守、別將蕭寶夤長史。

translations.literal: Student of the Palace Secretariat, Registrar to the Prince of Gaoyang of Xiang Province, Aide to the Prince of Guangling, Administrator of Xincai, and Chief Clerk to Separate Commander Xiao Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of the palace secretariat, registrar to the prince of Gaoyang of Xiang Province, aide to the prince of Guangling, administrator of Xincai, and chief clerk to separate commander Xiao Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 從中山王英破蕭衍臨川王蕭宏於梁城。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, in defeating Xiao Yan's Prince of Linchuan, Xiao Hong, at Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Ying of Zhongshan in defeating Xiao Yan's prince of Linchuan, Xiao Hong, at Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 除朔州安北府長史，又為中堅將軍、相州鎮北府長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Pacification-of-the-North Staff of Shuo Province, then served as General of the Central Fortress and Chief Clerk of the Defense-of-the-North Staff of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of the pacification-of-the-north staff of Shuo Province, then served as general of the central fortress and chief clerk of the defense-of-the-north staff of Xiang Province.
