sentences.zh: 遷冠軍將軍、魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Champions and Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who champions and administrator of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史、中山王熙據鄴起兵也，孝怡陰結募城民與熙長史柳元章、別駕游荊之等率眾擒熙，賞爵昌樂伯。

translations.literal: When the Governor of Xiang Province, the Prince of Zhongshan, Xi, rose in arms and seized Ye, Xiaoyi secretly gathered and enlisted city people; with Xi's Chief Clerk Liu Yuanzhang, Vice Governor You Jingzhi, and others he led the crowd to seize Xi and was rewarded with the title Marquis of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xi of Zhongshan, governor of Xiang Province, seized Ye and rose in revolt, Xiaoyi secretly recruited townspeople and, together with Xi's chief clerk Liu Yuanzhang, vice governor You Jingzhi, and others, led them to capture Xi; he was rewarded with the title marquis of Changle.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以孝怡叉黨，除名為民。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling returned to power, because Xiaoyi was a follower of Yuan Cha's faction he was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, Xiaoyi was removed from the rolls and reduced to commoner status as a member of Yuan Cha's faction.

sentences.zh: 後安樂王鑒鎮鄴，起孝怡為別將。

translations.literal: Later when the Prince of Anle, Jian, garrisoned Ye, he raised Xiaoyi to Separate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince Jian of Anle was posted to Ye, he appointed Xiaoyi separate commander.

sentences.zh: 永安初，除左將軍、太中大夫，仍為防城都督。

translations.literal: At the start of Yong'an he was appointed General of the Left and Grand Master of Palace, and continued as Commander overseeing city defense.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yong'an he was appointed general of the left and grand master of the palace, and continued as commander in charge of city defense.

sentences.zh: 以拒葛榮之勳，賜爵趙郡公，拜撫軍將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For merit in resisting Ge Rong he was granted the title Marquis of Zhao Commandery and appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in resisting Ge Rong he was enfeoffed as marquis of Zhao Commandery and appointed general who pacifies the army and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，行殷州事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he acted in the affairs of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he acted as administrator of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Pillar-General of the Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to pillar-general of the cavalry and left grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 武定六年卒，八十。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Wuding, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Wuding, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 子思道，儀同開府中兵參軍，武城縣公。

translations.literal: His son Sidao, Military Staff Officer of the Companionship-Equaling Open Office, Duke of Wucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sidao served as military staff officer in the companionship-equaling open office and held the title duke of Wucheng county.

sentences.zh: 熙，字仲熙。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Zhongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was styled Zhongxi.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，與高允等俱被徵，拜中書博士，轉侍郎。

translations.literal: During Shengui he was summoned together with Gao Yun and others, appointed Doctor of the Palace Secretariat, and transferred to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: During Shengui he was summoned together with Gao Yun and others, appointed doctor of the palace secretariat, and later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 以使沮渠有功，賜爵元氏子，加中壘將軍。

translations.literal: Because of merit on the mission to the Juqu he was granted the title Viscount of Yuanshi and given the additional rank General of the Central Ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: For merit on the mission against the Juqu he was granted the title viscount of Yuanshi and promoted to general of the central ramparts.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮東將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received the titles General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yu Province; his posthumous name was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the titles general who pacifies the east and governor of Yu Province, with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子季主，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jizhu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jizhu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received the title Governor of Qing Province; his posthumous name was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the title governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子遺元，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yiyuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiyuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 初除冀州趙郡王幹東閤祭酒，累轉尚書左民郎中、冀州京兆王愉功曹參軍，帶扶柳令。

translations.literal: He was first appointed East Pavilion Libationer to the Prince of Zhao Commandery of Ji Province, and by stages transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat's People Bureau, Staff Officer to the Prince of Jingzhao of Ji Province, and concurrently Magistrate of Fuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed east pavilion libationer to the prince of Zhao Commandery of Ji Province, then rose through the posts of gentleman of the secretariat's people bureau and staff officer to the prince of Jingzhao of Ji Province, while also serving as magistrate of Fuzhu.

sentences.zh: 為愉所親，逼與同反。

translations.literal: He was cherished by Yu, who compelled him to rebel together.
translations.idiomatic: Yu favored him and forced him to join the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 愉敗，遺元逃竄，會赦乃雪。

translations.literal: When Yu was defeated Yiyuan fled and hid; an amnesty then cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was defeated, Yiyuan fled into hiding and was cleared only when a general amnesty was issued.

sentences.zh: 復除兗州平東府長史。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Chief Clerk of the Eastern Pacification Office of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed chief clerk of the eastern pacification office of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 後拜中堅將軍、殷州征北將軍長史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Central Fortress and Chief Clerk of the Pacification-of-the-North General of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed general of the central fortress and chief clerk to the pacification-of-the-north general of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈征北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the titles general who pacifies the north and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子恃寧，以父事被刑。

translations.literal: His son Shining, because of his father's affair suffered mutilation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shining had been punished with mutilation on account of his father's case.

sentences.zh: 武定末，官至中尹。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he reached the post of Central Steward.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Wuding he had risen to central steward.

sentences.zh: 恃寧弟子寧，襲爵。

translations.literal: Shining's younger brother's son Ning inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Shining's nephew Ning inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 開府默曹參軍。

translations.literal: Staff Officer of the Silent Bureau of the Open Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer of the silent bureau in the open office.

sentences.zh: [11]齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: [11]When Qi received the abdication, his noble title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: [11]When Qi took the throne, his noble title was reduced in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 熙族孫蘭和，自右軍將軍歷平陽、勃海二郡太守。

translations.literal: Xi's clan grandson Lanhe, from General of the Right Army passed through the governorships of both Pingyang and Bohai commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's clan grandson Lanhe served from general of the right army through the governorships of Pingyang and Bohai commanderies.

sentences.zh: 蘭和弟蘭集，平昌太守。

translations.literal: Lanhe's younger brother Lanji, Administrator of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lanhe's younger brother Lanji was administrator of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 熙族孫同軌。

translations.literal: Xi's clan grandson Tonggui.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's clan grandson was Tonggui.

sentences.zh: [12]體貌魁岸，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: [12]His physique was lofty and imposing; his waist belt was ten spans in girth.
translations.idiomatic: [12]He was tall and imposing in bearing, with a waist ten spans around.

sentences.zh: 學綜諸經，多所治誦，兼讀釋氏，又好醫術。

translations.literal: His learning embraced the various classics, many of which he had mastered and recited; he also read Buddhist works and delighted in medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: He had mastered many of the classics through extensive study and recitation, read Buddhist texts as well, and was also fond of medicine.

sentences.zh: 年二十二，舉秀才，射策，除奉朝請，領國子助教。

translations.literal: At age twenty-two he was recommended as a cultivated talent, passed the target-shooting examination, was appointed Regular Attendant at Court, and concurrently served as Assistant Instructor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-two he was recommended as a cultivated talent, passed the archery examination, was appointed regular attendant at court, and concurrently served as assistant instructor of the national university.

sentences.zh: 轉著作郎，典儀注，修國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Composition Bureau, oversaw ritual protocols, and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the composition bureau, where he oversaw ritual protocols and worked on the national history.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor of the National University and given the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to doctor of the national university with the additional title general who subdues the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，出帝幸平等寺，僧徒講說，敕同軌論難，音韻閒朗，往復可觀，出帝善之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, the departed emperor (Chu-di) visited Pingdeng Temple; when the monks lectured, he ordered Tonggui to engage in debate. His tones were clear and serene, his exchanges polished and worth watching, and the departed emperor was pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongxi era, the emperor visited Pingdeng Temple. When the monks lectured, he ordered Tonggui to debate with them. Tonggui's voice was clear and measured, his exchanges polished and engaging, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 三年春釋菜，詔延公卿學官於顯陽殿，敕祭酒劉廞講孝經，黃門李郁講禮記，中書舍人盧景宣解大戴禮夏小正篇。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year, at the caiting ceremony, an edict summoned dukes, ministers, and academic officials to the Hall of Brilliant Yang. The libationer Liu Yin was commanded to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Huangmen Attendant Li Yu on the Record of Rites, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Jingxuan to explicate the "Xia Xiaozheng" section of Dai the Elder's Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year, at the vegetable-offering ceremony, an edict summoned the nobles and academic officials to the Hall of Brilliant Yang. The libationer Liu Yin was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Huangmen attendant Li Yu on the Record of Rites, and secretariat gentleman Lu Jingxuan to explicate the "Xia Xiaozheng" chapter of the Elder Dai's Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時廣招儒學，引令預聽。

translations.literal: At that time Confucian scholars were widely recruited, and he was invited to attend and listen in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars were being recruited widely at the time, and he was invited to join the audience.

sentences.zh: 同軌經義素優，辯析兼美，而不得執經，深為慨恨。

translations.literal: Tonggui had long excelled in scriptural interpretation and was also gifted at analysis and disputation, yet he was not allowed to hold the lectern—a source of deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui had long excelled in classical interpretation and was equally gifted at analysis and debate, yet he was not permitted to hold the lectern, which he deeply regretted.

sentences.zh: 天平中，[13]轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: During Tianping, [13] he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era, [13] he was transferred to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 興和中，兼通直散騎常侍，使蕭衍。

translations.literal: During Xinghe, he also served as Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Office of the Imperial Secretariat and went as envoy to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era he also served as regular attendant of the unimpeded office of the imperial secretariat and went as envoy to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍深耽釋學，遂集名僧於其愛敬、同泰二寺，講湼槃大品經，引同軌預席，衍兼遣其臣並共觀聽。

translations.literal: Yan was deeply devoted to Buddhist learning. He therefore gathered eminent monks at his temples of Ai'ai and Tongtai to lecture on the Mahaparinirvana Sutra of the Great Vehicle, invited Tonggui to join the assembly, and also sent his ministers to watch and listen together.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was deeply devoted to Buddhist studies. He gathered eminent monks at his Ai'ai and Tongtai temples to lecture on the Mahaparinirvana Sutra, invited Tonggui to take part, and also sent his ministers to attend and listen.

sentences.zh: 同軌論難久之，道俗咸以為善。

translations.literal: Tonggui debated at length; clergy and laity alike judged it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui debated at length, and clergy and laity alike praised his performance.

sentences.zh: 盧景裕卒，齊獻武王引同軌在館教諸公子，甚嘉禮之，每旦入授，日暮始歸。

translations.literal: When Lu Jingyu died, Prince Xianwu of Qi brought Tonggui into his residence to teach the princes' sons, treating him with great courtesy and kindness. Each morning he entered to instruct them and did not return home until evening.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Jingyu died, Prince Xianwu of Qi brought Tonggui into his household to teach the princes' sons, treating him with exceptional courtesy. Each morning he arrived to instruct them and did not return home until evening.

sentences.zh: 緇素請業者，同軌夜為解說，四時恒爾，不以為倦。

translations.literal: When monks and laymen sought instruction, Tonggui explained for them at night—through all four seasons he did this constantly and never regarded it as wearisome.
translations.idiomatic: When monks and laymen came seeking instruction, Tonggui would explain for them at night. He did this through all four seasons without ever growing weary.

sentences.zh: 武定四年夏卒，年四十七，時人傷惜之。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year of Wuding he died, aged forty-seven, and people of the time mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the fourth year of Wuding, at the age of forty-seven, and people of the time mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王亦殊嗟悼，賻襚甚厚。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi also grieved him with special sorrow, and his funeral gifts and burial regalia were very lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi also grieved him deeply and sent very lavish funeral gifts and burial regalia.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、瀛州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the titles General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Ying Province, and posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the titles general of agile cavalry and governor of Ying Province, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 同軌兄義深，武定中，齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Tonggui's elder brother Yishen, during Wuding, was governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui's elder brother Yishen was governor of Qi Province during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 同軌弟幼舉，安德太守。

translations.literal: Tonggui's younger brother Youju was administrator of Ande.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui's younger brother Youju was administrator of Ande.

sentences.zh: 武定中，以在郡貪汙，輒召部曲還京師，棄市。

translations.literal: During Wuding, for corruption while in his command, he was immediately summoned back to the capital with his personal troops and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era, for corruption in his commandery, he was immediately summoned back to the capital with his personal troops and executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 幼舉弟之良，有幹用。

translations.literal: Youju's younger brother Zhiliang was capable and useful.
translations.idiomatic: Youju's younger brother Zhiliang was capable and effective.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: Former General; Gentleman of the Secretariat, Gold Section.
translations.idiomatic: He served as former general and gentleman of the secretariat, gold section.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 之良弟稚廉，武定末，并州儀同開府長史。

translations.literal: Zhiliang's younger brother Zhilian, at the end of Wuding, was senior aide to the Office with the prestige of equal to the Three Excellencies in Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiliang's younger brother Zhilian, at the end of the Wuding era, was senior aide to the office with the prestige of equal to the three excellencies in Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李順器宇才識，一時推重，謀宣中國，氣折外蕃。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Li Shun's bearing and talent were esteemed by his age; his plans proclaimed them to the Central Domain, and his spirit broke the outer tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Li Shun's bearing and talent won the esteem of his age; his counsel advanced the Central Domain, and his spirit humbled the outer tribes.

sentences.zh: 所以世祖垂心，而崔浩側目。

translations.literal: Therefore the Shizu Emperor turned his heart to him, while Cui Hao looked on askance.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Emperor Shizu favored him, while Cui Hao looked on with resentment.

sentences.zh: 敷式兄弟，位望並高。

translations.literal: The brothers Fu and Shi—rank and fame were both lofty.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Fu and Shi both rose to high rank and renown.

sentences.zh: 憲風度恢雅，夙重朝列。

translations.literal: Xian's bearing was broad and refined; from of old he was weighty in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's bearing was broad and refined; from of old he was held in high regard at court.

sentences.zh: 而遭隨有命，報施俱爽。

translations.literal: Yet he met with fate ordained by the age that followed, and reward and requital alike failed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he met with the fate ordained by the age that followed, and reward and requital alike went unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 以茲盛德，克廣其猷，宗緒扶疏，人位盛顯，可謂李雖舊族，其世唯新矣。

translations.literal: With such abundant virtue he could have broadened their designs; the lineage flourished and spread, men and offices rose to eminence—one may say that though the Li were an old clan, their age alone was ever new.
translations.idiomatic: With such abundant virtue they might have broadened their designs; the lineage flourished and spread, and men and offices rose to eminence. One may say that though the Li were an old clan, their age was ever new.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 似窮桑之世濟 諸本「桑」作「葉」，獨局本作「桑」。

translations.literal: "As if aiding the age of the Exhausted Mulberry": in all editions "mulberry" (桑) is written "leaf" (葉); only the Bureau edition has "mulberry."
translations.idiomatic: "As if aiding the age of the exhausted mulberry": in all editions "mulberry" is written "leaf"; only the Bureau edition reads mulberry.

sentences.zh: 按左傳昭二十九年蔡墨稱少皡氏有四叔，「世不失職，遂濟窮桑」，賦用此典故。

translations.literal: According to the Zuo Commentary, Duke Zhao year 29, Cai Mo said that Shaohao's clan had four uncles who "never lost their offices generation after generation and thus aided the exhausted mulberry"—the fu-rhapsody uses this allusion.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Zuo Commentary (Duke Zhao, year 29), Cai Mo said that Shaohao's clan had four uncles who "never lost their offices from generation to generation and thus aided the exhausted mulberry"—the fu-rhapsody draws on this allusion.

sentences.zh: 今從局本。

translations.literal: The text now follows the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: The text now follows the Bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 求班莊而不遂 按「班莊」不知所出。

translations.literal: "Seeking Ban [Gu] and Zhuang [???] yet not attaining": according to this passage, the origin of "Ban Zhuang" is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: "Seeking Ban and Zhuang yet not attaining": the source of "Ban Zhuang" is unknown.

sentences.zh: 前幾句都說讀書事，後漢書卷四０班固傳，稱固讀書禁中，或即指此，但「莊」字不可解，疑字訛。

translations.literal: The preceding lines all concern reading books. The biography of Ban Gu in Hou Han shu chapter 40 says Gu read in the Forbidden Quarter—perhaps that is what is meant, but the character "Zhuang" cannot be explained and is probably a corrupted character.
translations.idiomatic: The preceding lines all concern reading. The biography of Ban Gu in Hou Han shu chapter 40 says that Gu read in the Forbidden Quarter—perhaps that is what is meant—but the character Zhuang cannot be explained and is probably a corruption.

sentences.zh: 若謝兼之來仕 按後漢書卷六一左雄傳稱：「汝南謝廉、河南趙建年始十二，各能通經，雄並奏拜童子郎。

translations.literal: "Like Xie Jian coming to office": according to the biography of Zuo Xiong in Hou Han shu chapter 61: "Xie Lian of Runan and Zhao Jian of Henan, at the age of twelve each could master the classics; Xiong memorialized and appointed them both Boy Attendants."
translations.idiomatic: "Like Xie Jian coming to office": according to the biography of Zuo Xiong in Hou Han shu chapter 61: "Xie Lian of Runan and Zhao Jian of Henan, at the age of twelve, each could master the classics; Xiong memorialized and appointed them both boy attendants."

sentences.zh: 」上云：「騫年十四，國子學生」，事類謝廉，故以此為比。

translations.literal: " Above it says, "[Li] Qian at age fourteen was a student of the National University"; the matter is analogous to Xie Lian, hence this comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Above it says, "Qian at age fourteen was a student of the national university"; the case is analogous to Xie Lian, hence this comparison.

sentences.zh: 「兼」當是「廉」之訛，否則後漢書「兼」訛「廉」。

translations.literal: "Jian" must be a corruption of "Lian," or else Hou Han shu has "Jian" corrupted from "Lian."
translations.idiomatic: Jian must be a corruption of Lian; otherwise Hou Han shu has Jian corrupted from Lian.

sentences.zh: 益州達友趣 諸本「友」作「反」，北史卷三三李騫傳作「友」。

translations.literal: "The friendship-trend of Yizhou Prefecture": in all editions "friend" (友) is written "reverse" (反); Beishi chapter 33, biography of Li Qian, has "friend."
translations.idiomatic: "The friendship-trend of Yizhou": in all editions "friend" is written "reverse"; the biography of Li Qian in Beishi chapter 33 reads friend.

sentences.zh: 按漢書卷七二王吉傳云：「吉與貢禹為友，世稱『王陽

translations.literal: According to Han shu chapter 72, biography of Wang Ji, it says: "Ji and Gong Yu were friends; the age called them 'Wang Yang
translations.idiomatic: According to Han shu chapter 72, biography of Wang Ji: "Ji and Gong Yu were friends; the age called them 'Wang Yang

sentences.zh: 〈即吉〉

translations.literal: (i.e., Ji)
translations.idiomatic: (i.e., Ji)

sentences.zh: 在位，貢公彈冠』，言其取舍同也。

translations.literal: in office, Lord Gong dusted his cap,'" meaning their choices were the same.
translations.idiomatic: in office, Lord Gong dusted his cap,'" meaning their choices were alike.

sentences.zh: 」王吉曾官益州刺史，故稱他為「益州」。

translations.literal: " Wang Ji once served as governor of Yizhou, hence he is called "Yizhou."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji once served as governor of Yizhou, hence he is called "Yizhou."

sentences.zh: 御覽卷四０六

translations.literal: Yulan chapter 406
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings (Yulan), chapter 406

sentences.zh: 〈一八七九頁〉
引漢書，說王吉為益州刺史時薦貢禹，今漢書本傳無此語，或是誤引，但也可證此詩用的是王吉、貢禹事。

translations.literal: cites Han shu, saying that when Wang Ji was governor of Yizhou he recommended Gong Yu; the present biography in Han shu lacks this passage—perhaps it is a mistaken citation, but it also shows that this poem uses the story of Wang Ji and Gong Yu.
translations.idiomatic: cites Han shu, saying that when Wang Ji was governor of Yizhou he recommended Gong Yu. The present Han shu biography lacks this passage—it may be a mistaken citation—but it also shows that this poem draws on the story of Wang Ji and Gong Yu.

sentences.zh: 「反」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "reverse" is corrupt; the text is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The character fan (reverse) is corrupt; the text is now emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 希遠庶長兄長劍 北、汲、殿、局四本「長劍」單作「劍」，百衲本、南本作「長劍」。

translations.literal: "Xiyuan's eldest son by a concubine, elder brother Changjian": in the Bei, Ji, Dian, and Bureau editions "Changjian" appears alone as "Jian"; the Patchwork and Southern editions have "Changjian."
translations.idiomatic: "Xiyuan's eldest son by a concubine, elder brother Changjian": in the Bei, Ji, Dian, and Bureau editions Changjian appears alone as Jian; the Patchwork and Southern editions read Changjian.

sentences.zh: 北史卷三三、墓誌集釋李憲墓誌記李憲諸子皆無此人。

translations.literal: Beishi chapter 33 and the collected exegesis of epitaphs, epitaph of Li Xian, record none of Li Xian's sons as this person.
translations.idiomatic: Beishi chapter 33 and the epitaph of Li Xian in the collected exegesis of epitaphs list none of Li Xian's sons as this person.

sentences.zh: 檢上文於騫子希遠下記「希遠兄長鈞，興和中，梁州驃騎府長史」。

translations.literal: Checking the text above, under Qian's son Xiyuan it records "Xiyuan's elder brother Changjun, during Xinghe, senior aide of the Agile Cavalry Office in Liang Province."
translations.idiomatic: Checking the text above, under Qian's son Xiyuan it records "Xiyuan's elder brother Changjun, during Xinghe, senior aide of the agile cavalry office in Liang Province."

sentences.zh: 長鈞是希遠兄，却排在希遠後，墓誌亦同，說明其為庶長子。

translations.literal: Changjun was Xiyuan's elder brother yet is listed after Xiyuan; the epitaph is the same, showing that he was the eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Changjun was Xiyuan's elder brother yet is listed after Xiyuan; the epitaph agrees, showing that he was the eldest son by a concubine.

sentences.zh: 時、地、官位又全與長劍同。

translations.literal: Time, place, and office are also entirely the same as Changjian's.
translations.idiomatic: The time, place, and office are also entirely the same as Changjian's.

sentences.zh: 八瓊室金石補正卷一八、越縵堂文集卷七跋李憲墓誌都認為長鈞、長劍實是一人，魏書誤分為二。

translations.literal: Baqiong Studio's Supplement to Metal and Stone, chapter 18, and the colophon to Li Xian's epitaph in Yue Mantang's collected works, chapter 7, both hold that Changjun and Changjian were in fact one person and that the Book of Wei mistakenly divided them into two.
translations.idiomatic: Supplement to Metal and Stone (Baqiong Studio), chapter 18, and the colophon to Li Xian's epitaph in Yue Mantang's collected works, chapter 7, both hold that Changjun and Changjian were in fact one person and that the Book of Wei mistakenly split them into two.

sentences.zh: 按魏收是長鈞弟李騫的「親友」

translations.literal: According to this, Wei Shou was the "close friend" of Changjun's younger brother Li Qian
translations.idiomatic: According to this, Wei Shou was the "close friend" of Changjun's younger brother Li Qian

sentences.zh: 〈見上騫傳〉

translations.literal: (see the biography of Qian above)
translations.idiomatic: (see the biography of Qian above)

sentences.zh: ，不致謬誤至此。

translations.literal: , and would not have erred to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: , and would not have erred to this degree.

sentences.zh: 疑他書「長鈞」偶訛「長劍」，後人以為二人，妄加此一行。

translations.literal: It is suspected that in another text "Changjun" was occasionally corrupted to "Changjian," and later people took them for two men and added this line without warrant.
translations.idiomatic: It is suspected that in another text Changjun was occasionally corrupted to Changjian, and later readers took them for two men and added this line without warrant.

sentences.zh: 存問憲等一二家 按「一二家」當是「三家」之訛，指李順子敷、式、弈三家，或敷兄弟與從弟顯德、妹夫宋叔珍三家。

translations.literal: "Inquiring after Xian and the one or two households": according to this, "one or two households" should be a corruption of "three households," referring to the three households of Li Shun's sons Fu, Shi, and Yi—or the three households of the Fu brothers together with their cousin Xiande and brother-in-law Song Shuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: "Inquiring after Xian and the one or two households": "one or two households" should be a corruption of "three households," referring either to the three households of Li Shun's sons Fu, Shi, and Yi, or to the Fu brothers together with their cousin Xiande and brother-in-law Song Shuzhen.

sentences.zh: 事見上文李敷傳。

translations.literal: The matter is seen in the biography of Li Fu above.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is described in the biography of Li Fu above.

sentences.zh: 事在高允高士頌 李慈銘云：「『高士』當從北史作『徵士』。」

translations.literal: "The matter is in Gao Yun's Eulogy of Lofty Scholars": Li Ciming says: "'Lofty scholar' should follow Beishi and be written 'recluse scholar.'"
translations.idiomatic: "The matter is in Gao Yun's Eulogy of Lofty Scholars": Li Ciming says, "Lofty scholar should follow Beishi and read recluse scholar."

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節大將軍陝州刺史 北史卷三三李裔傳，「大將軍」上有「候衞」二字。

translations.literal: "Soon removed to Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Governor of Shan Province": in Beishi chapter 33, biography of Li Yi, above "Grand General" are the two characters "Garrison Guard."
translations.idiomatic: "Soon appointed bearer of the staff, grand general, and governor of Shan Province": in the biography of Li Yi in Beishi chapter 33, the two characters "garrison guard" appear above "grand general."

sentences.zh: 按李裔軍號先止「征東將軍」第二品，死後贈官是「驃騎大將軍」從第一品，不可能此時給以大將軍

translations.literal: According to this, Li Yi's military title had previously stopped at "General Who Campaigns East," second rank; his posthumous gift was "General of Agile Cavalry," sub-first rank—it was impossible at this time to grant the title Grand General
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi's military title had previously been only general who campaigns east, second rank; his posthumous gift was general of agile cavalry, sub-first rank. He could not at this time have been given the title grand general

translations.literal: But in early Eastern Wei there was also no office of "Garrison Guard Grand General."
translations.idiomatic: But in early Eastern Wei there was also no office of garrison guard grand general.

sentences.zh: 疑是「衞大將軍」，此傳脫「衞」字，北史衍「候」字。

translations.literal: It is suspected that the title was "Guard Grand General"; this biography omits the character "Guard," and Beishi adds the character "Garrison."
translations.idiomatic: The title was probably guard grand general; this biography omits Guard, while Beishi adds Garrison.

sentences.zh: 按隋書卷四六李雄傳也作「子旦」，這裏當脫「子」字，「旦」訛「直」。

translations.literal: According to this, the biography of Li Xiong in Suishu chapter 46 also has "Zidan"; here the character "Zi" was probably omitted and "Dan" was corrupted to "Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Li Xiong in Suishu chapter 46 also reads Zidan; here the character zi was probably omitted and dan was corrupted to zhi.

translations.idiomatic: "Making Zhongwan director of works for construction": the main biography in Beishi chapter 33 lacks the character for works.

translations.idiomatic: The original probably read "construction commander," with "in-chief" omitted, matching Beishi, and the character for works is an addition.

sentences.zh: 開府默曹參軍 按「默曹」當作「墨曹」，隋書卷二七百官志中稱北齊三師、二大、三公府屬官有「法、墨、田、水、鎧、集、士等曹行參軍」。

translations.literal: "Staff Officer of the Silent Section of the Office": according to this, "Silent Section" should be "Ink Section." The offices table in Suishu chapter 27 says that under the Northern Qi the three preceptors, two grand tutors, and the three excellencies' offices had staff officers of the law, ink, field, water, armor, collection, and scholar sections, among others.
translations.idiomatic: "Staff officer of the silent section of the office": "silent section" should read "ink section." Suishu chapter 27, offices table, states that under the Northern Qi the three preceptors, two grand tutors, and the three excellencies' offices had staff officers of the law, ink, field, water, armor, collection, and scholar sections, among others.

sentences.zh: 儀同三司加開府也有諸曹屬官，雖有減少，墨曹却未減。

translations.literal: An office with the prestige of equal to the Three Excellencies that also opened a bureau likewise had subordinate officials of the various sections; though some were reduced, the Ink Section was not reduced.
translations.idiomatic: An office with the prestige of equal to the three excellencies that also opened a bureau likewise had subordinate officials of the various sections; though some were reduced, the ink section was not.

sentences.zh: 北齊當因魏制。

translations.literal: Northern Qi presumably followed Wei institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi presumably followed Wei institutions.

sentences.zh: 魏書中「墨曹」常作「默曹」，今不改，以後也不再出校記。

translations.literal: In the Book of Wei "Ink Section" is often written "Silent Section"; it is not emended here, and no further collation notes on this will be given.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Wei "ink section" is often written "silent section"; it is not emended here, and no further collation notes on this will be given.

sentences.zh: 熙族孫同軌 按卷八四儒林傳也有同軌傳，除傳首不同及傳末無「同軌弟幼舉」外，文字全同，實是一人二傳，參卷八四校記[一]。

translations.literal: "Xi's clan grandson Tonggui": according to this, chapter 84, Confucian Scholars, also has a biography of Tonggui; apart from a different opening and the absence at the end of "Tonggui's younger brother Youju," the text is entirely the same—it is in fact one man with two biographies. See collation note [1] in chapter 84.
translations.idiomatic: "Xi's clan grandson Tonggui": chapter 84, Confucian Scholars, also has a biography of Tonggui. Apart from a different opening and the absence at the end of "Tonggui's younger brother Youju," the text is identical—it is one man entered twice. See collation note [1] in chapter 84.
